《上海泰晤士报》
14077
1939年6月4日

经济上海与犹太移民
 newcomers 将在大都市生活中扮演什么角色？——维克多·沙逊爵士访谈；巨大的救济工作

作者：阿瑟和西奥多·索弗（Arthur and Theodore Sopher）

不到两年前，从上海出发的船只挤满了寻求远离空袭和包围战火的避难者。当时谁能想到，在短短的时间内，这个港口竟会成为更多人的避风港，如今这些人正填满每一个可用的舱位来到这里？曾经要逃离的城市变成了争相涌入的地方。在如此短的时期内，对上海的厌恶转变为如此深厚的喜爱，这似乎显得不够理智。然而，属于这里的人们早已习惯了这座大都市一再展现出的这种独特的恢复活力。

纵观这个港口非凡且充满事件的历史，种种原因和结果共同导致了公民和经济发展的上升趋势。虽然不对我们有利局势的性质和原因提供解释，但可以观察到，上海内部的架构因其复杂性，似乎以某种方式抵御了迫在眉睫的危险，并将麻烦转化为利益。

迄今为止，几个国籍作为组成部分，融合成了一个构成我们上海的联合体。这里信奉犹太教的人数（约3,500人），约占非中国人口总数（约70,000人）的百分之五，分布在各个国籍群体中，其中大部分犹太人是20年前随着白俄难民的大批涌入而来的。因此，在这百分之五的人口中，只有四分之三个百分点，即500人，是随城市早期定居者而来的英国及其他国籍的犹太人家庭后裔。

避难所

纯粹由于政治环境的力量，比例相当大的德国和奥地利犹太人现在被迫将这些海岸作为避难所。若非政治上的偶然，他们绝不会来到这里。这个世界地区的商业性质并不是吸引这些人来到我们城市的因素，因为他们原本在原地生活安逸。上海吸引他们仅仅是因为没有其他地方可以提供必要的入境通道。

在大约25万名从大德意志地区移民或死亡的人中，15万人去了海外，其余去了欧洲国家，约4.5万人去了巴勒斯坦，还有相当数量的人去了美洲大陆的不同国家。英国自治领和殖民地也吸收了一定数量，自去年年底以来，英国成为主要的即时避难国。在那里，一个最具影响力的救济组织已经成立，旨在为移民事务提供建设性帮助，并将移民由此分发到海外。1933年至1939年间，英国筹集了超过200万英镑。

pages.en:
14078
Why Shanghai Was Chosen
From the foregoing facts it is obvious that Shanghai is not being singled out as a dumping-ground, and that these unfortunate emigrants from Greater Germany have come, by the logic of circumstance, along this path. On account of the liberal principles in this regard exercised by several powerful nations in Shanghai as one body —British, French, American and Japanese—it is possible for them to arrive here. The Chinese people have always been the most tolerant in the matter of race and creed. And in such respect, it is to be called to mind that Jewish merchants as far back as 200 B.C. were using the overland route via Turkestan to Kaifengfu—then the capital of China. They were largely traffickers in silk, which was in great demand for the adornment of wealthy Roman women. The open-mindedness of Ancient Cathay was shown in the fact that a large colony of Jews settled there, founded Synagogues and spread all over the length and breath of the land. By the time Marco Polo arrived (circa 1200 A.D.) he found them in official positions and in the Mandarinate at Peking, Chingkiang, and the-then glorious queen-city of Hangchow. It is worthy of particular note that the peoples of China were the greatest exercisers of the spirit of religious toleration, for these ancient Jewish colonists here were treated with such admirable equality that the Jews became completely absorbed into the population. It is true that to-day they are remnants at Kaifengfu, but they are indistinguishable in appearance from the Chinese themselves.
Two Schools Of Thought
The authorities in Japan are now making a special study of the Jewish question, and two schools of thought have arisen—one for and one against. Professor T. Shibata has written an important book on the subject strongly in favour of Jews and was recently visiting places in China and Shanghai to collect data to report to Premier Hiranuma. It is of great importance that the Japanese are taking such an extraordinary interest in the subject, and much shrewdness is being revealed by them in trying to come to the right conclusions. Moreover, leading Japanese visiting Shanghai are taking particular pains to make inquiries on the matter to report to the Home Government, and they are treating it as a subject of paramount interest to them.
This is not without good reason. And here some of the findings will prove useful as a guide to Shanghai.
Wherever the Jews settled, the bald record shows that they were an asset in every way. The Jews, being a people of a religion, not of a particular land or territory, are naturally internationally-minded, and there is no difficulty for them whatever to give of their utmost in loyalty and allegiance to whichever land there is that extends hospitality and protection to them. This fact has been proved and attested in an untold number of instances, over periods of time measured not by short years but by long centuries. In war, their patriotism, to the different countries of their adoption, proved equal to their fellow-nationals, and they made the supreme sacrifice in no less a proportion to the general population.
pages.zh:
14078

为何选择上海

从前述事实可以看出，上海并非被 singled out 作为倾倒垃圾之地，这些来自大德意志地区的不幸移民是顺着环境的逻辑沿着这条路径而来的。由于在上海作为一个整体行使权力的几个强国——英国、法国、美国和日本——在这方面奉行自由主义原则，使他们得以抵达这里。中国人民在种族和信仰问题上一直是最宽容的。在这方面，值得回想的是，早在公元前200年，犹太商人就利用经由突厥斯坦通往开封府（当时是中国的首都）的陆路路线。他们主要是丝绸贩运商，而丝绸在富裕的罗马妇女装饰方面需求巨大。古代中国的开明态度体现在大量犹太殖民者在此定居，建立会堂，并遍布全国各地。当马可·波罗到达时（约公元1200年），他发现他们在北京、镇江以及当时辉煌的皇后之城杭州担任官职并在官场任职。特别值得注意的是，中国人民是宗教宽容精神的最大践行者，因为这些古老的犹太殖民者在这里受到了令人钦佩的平等对待，以至于犹太人完全融入了当地人口。的确，今天他们在开封府已是残存群体，但在外貌上与中国人本身已无法区分。

两种思想流派

日本当局目前正在专门研究犹太问题，并出现了两种思想流派——一派支持，一派反对。T. Shibata 教授就此主题写了一本重要著作，强烈支持犹太人，最近正在中国和上海各地访问，收集数据以向平沼首相报告。日本人对这一主题表现出如此非同寻常的兴趣，这一点至关重要，他们在试图得出正确结论的过程中展现出了极大的精明。此外，访问上海的日本知名人士正特别费力地就此事项进行调查，以便向本国政府报告，并将其视为对他们至关重要的议题。

这并非没有充分理由。在此，一些调查结果将被证明对上海具有指导作用。

无论犹太人在哪里定居，赤裸裸的记录显示，他们在各方面都是一笔资产。犹太人是一个宗教民族，而非特定土地或领土的民族，自然具有国际视野，他们毫不困难地对任何向他们提供款待和保护的土地竭尽忠诚和效忠。这一事实在无数实例中得到了证明和证实，其时间跨度不是以短暂的年份计算，而是以漫长的世纪衡量。在战争中，他们对不同收养国的爱国主义精神证明与其同胞不相上下，他们做出 supreme sacrifice 的比例也不低于一般人口。

pages.en:
14079

Jews As Trade Pioneers
The original core of Shanghai Jews came out with the expansion of British trading interests from India to China, a 100 years ago. Among the pioneer British firms was that of Sassoon—a name synonymous in the East with 'he world-famed banking house of Rothschild, in Europe and England. The Sassoons originated from that once-great city of culture and commerce—Baghdad—the resplendent jewel of the Moslem world.' The family, with many others, had been settled in the Mesopotamian centre for several centuries, having, it is said, come there via Italy and Constantinople from the fierce persecutions in Spain in the time of the notorious Torquemada.
For ages, this distinguished family of Sassoon took a leading part in general business and Jewish communal interests. They were like a river of life for their co-religionists, and the family's principal characteristic has been devotion to the public good. This is the main secret of their greatness. The public record, alongside their commercial development, has been one long story of philanthropic endeavour. The business benefit that they had gotten for themselves is only a mere fraction of the abundance that they brought to others through their services.
The House Of Sassoon
To-day, the House of Sassoon in China, is represented in the person of Sir Victor Sassoon, Baronet, who during the Great War volunteered as an aviator, having then sustained permanent physical injury. Soon after the War was over, and becoming the principal inheritor from his uncle, Sir Jacob Sassoon, Bt., and later from his father, Sir Edward Sassoon, he took an active part himself in the commercial world of India, Hongkong, and China. His enterprise was to a certain extent concentrated at Shanghai, and it is to his spirit of progress that Shanghai owes some of its most luxurious and beautiful buildings together with numerous business organizations in different fields here.
At the present moment, Sir Victor Sassoon has rallied in a royal spirit to the dire cause of the Jewish immigrants of Shanghai. His personal enthusiasm for them, his energy, and his example is attracting many volunteers. And in this direction, several Jewish families, and some of distinction, have come forward in astounding manner from the very outset of the misfortune that befell their co-religionists and those partly of Jewish faith (inclusive of persons married to Jews and so-called "non-Aryans," Christians, and others who have one Jewish grandparent.) Noteworthy is it that Dr. Kurt Marx, who is greatly responsible for the refugee organization in Shanghai, originated its remarkably efficient regimental-like character for handling the problem in a practical way. Though he has been in indifferent health, this worthy gentleman (of Rudyard Kipling appearance, a four-year war-veteran and himself an early refugee from Germany arriving here some years back) has exerted superhuman dynamic energy, inspired as much by the urgent cause itself as by the responsiveness of his own indomitable nature.
pages.zh:
14079

犹太人作为贸易先驱

上海犹太人的最初核心是随着一百年前英国贸易利益从印度向中国的扩张而来的。在早期的英国商行中，有沙逊洋行（Sassoon）——这个名字在东方等同于欧洲和英国的世界著名银行家族罗斯柴尔德（Rothschild）。沙逊家族起源于那座曾经伟大的文化与商业之城——巴格达，即穆斯林世界璀璨的明珠。据说，该家族与许多其他家族一样，在美索不达米亚中心定居了几个世纪，他们是在臭名昭著的托尔克马达（Torquemada）时期，为躲避西班牙的残酷迫害，经由意大利和君士坦丁堡来到那里的。

多年来，这个显赫的沙逊家族在一般商业和犹太社区事务中发挥了主导作用。对于他们的教友来说，他们就像一条生命之河，而该家族的主要特征是对公共利益的奉献。这是他们伟大的主要秘密。除了商业发展外，他们的公共记录也是一部漫长的慈善努力史。他们为自己获得的商业利益，只是他们通过服务为他人带来的丰富成果中的一小部分。

沙逊洋行

如今，沙逊洋行在中国的代表人物是维克多·沙逊爵士（Sir Victor Sassoon），男爵。他在大战期间自愿担任飞行员，并因此遭受了永久性的身体伤害。战争结束后不久，他成为其叔父雅各布·沙逊爵士（Sir Jacob Sassoon, Bt.）以及后来其父爱德华·沙逊爵士（Sir Edward Sassoon）的主要继承人，随后亲自积极参与印度、香港和中国的商业界。他的企业活动在某种程度上集中于上海，上海一些最豪华美丽的建筑以及这里各个领域的众多商业组织，都要归功于他的进取精神。

目前，维克多·沙逊爵士以崇高的精神团结起来，投身于上海犹太移民的严峻事业中。他对他们的个人热情、精力和榜样作用正在吸引许多志愿者。在这方面，自从不幸降临到他们的教友以及部分具有犹太信仰的人（包括与犹太人结婚的人以及所谓的“非雅利安人”、基督徒和其他拥有一位犹太祖父母的人）身上之初，就有几个犹太家庭，其中一些颇具声望，以惊人的方式挺身而出。值得注意的是，库尔特·马克思博士（Dr. Kurt Marx）对上海的难民组织负有重大责任，他赋予了该组织显著的高效的军团式特征，以便以务实的方式处理这一问题。尽管这位可敬的绅士（外貌酷似鲁德亚德·吉卜林，是一位四年战龄的老兵，也是早期从德国抵达此地的难民，于几年前来到这里）健康状况不佳，但他发挥了超人的活力，这既源于事业本身的紧迫性，也源于他那不屈不挠的天性所激发的响应能力。

pages.en:
Strength Of Immigrants
Up to the time of writing, the total of immigrants has reached some 10,000 odd souls, and according to a speech reported in the Press of May 12, 1939, Sir Victor estimates that the aggregate of refugees, by the end of the year, would be about 25,000, swelling the total non-Chinese inhabitants of Shanghai to over 100,000. Analyzing the latter figure, we have some 40,000 Japanese, 25,000 'White' Russians, and an estimated 20,000 British, American, French and others, plus now the European immigrants. With the 3½ or 4 million Chinese population, the Settlement and Concession and Greater Shanghai, have now reached a new peak in population growth. Despite the sudden influx of non-Chinese arrivals, the ratio of foreigners to Chinese remains peculiarly unchanged at about 2½ per cent.
Now, the usefulness of our city of Shanghai is in a miscellany of services, comprised mainly of the following:—Commerce, shipping, storage, industry, banking, insurance and hostelry. The emphasis is now shifting towards industrial development and housing for all purposes. At the present moment, the great city's industry is yielding in some cases the greatest profits ever made, and real estate requirements, on account of past mistakes in finance and politico-legal disabilities, cannot cope with an utterly unprecedented demand for space.

Pertinent Question
The question is what part can these new Jewish immigrants play in the present and future growth of the city. It is, of course, well-known that generally speaking—supported by overwhelming evidence—Jewish settlers have always been producers. They are givers, not takers. Even in the case of these Jewish refugees, most of the funds have come from abroad and from the Jews here. They have been no charge whatever on the general community.
The problem is how are they going to fit in fast enough. In the first place, a good number are looking upon Shanghai as only a landing-ground of temporary residence, from where they hope to find their way to other parts of the world, more suitable to their absorption. However, a certain nucleus will always remain here, composed of those elements that can be constructive, such as industrialists, chemists, physicians, teachers, artisans, and technicians of all kinds. The great difficulty will be to bridge them over to such time as they will fit in with the city's scheme of things and to do that gradually.
Whilst it cannot be denied that life will become a little bit more under pressure and more competitive, still there is a variety of activity being opened by the immigrants, enterprises, new to Shanghai, in certain technical and trading articles, lines which are not at conflict with existing ones. In any event, the city has such potentialities that the future will see them in appropriate vocations.

A Note Of Hope
The most hopeful feature of all is that when people come together in a large body, and harmonize, they can pool skills, and resources, and create something. In the case of these refugees, though deprived of means, their union and co-ordination, spurred on by the sharp pinch of necessity, is bound to be productive and beneficial to the city, provided that their co-religionists, friends and sympathisers, here and all over the world, can first preserve their existence, so that they can be tided over to the better period that is sure to come.

14080
pages.zh:
移民的力量

截至撰写本文时，移民总数已达到约一万余人。根据1939年5月12日报纸报道的一次演讲，维克多爵士估计，到年底难民总数将达到约25,000人，使上海的非中国居民总数超过100,000人。分析后一数字，我们有约40,000名日本人，25,000名“白”俄国人，估计有20,000名英国人、美国人、法国人及其他人士，再加上现在的欧洲移民。随着三百五十万至四百万的中国人口，租界、公租界和大上海地区的人口增长现已达到一个新的高峰。尽管非中国籍人员突然涌入，但外国人与中国人的比例仍奇特般地保持在约2.5%不变。

现在，我们上海这座城市的作用体现在各种服务中，主要包括：商业、航运、仓储、工业、银行、保险和旅馆业。目前的重点正转向工业发展和各类住房建设。目前，这座大城市的工业在某些情况下产生了前所未有的最大利润，而由于过去的金融错误和政治法律上的障碍，房地产需求无法应对空间方面完全前所未有的需求。

相关问题

问题是这些新的犹太移民能在城市当前和未来的发展中发挥什么作用。当然，众所周知，一般来说——有压倒性的证据支持——犹太定居者一直是生产者。他们是给予者，而不是索取者。即使是对于这些犹太难民，大部分资金也来自国外和当地的犹太人。他们没有给普通社区带来任何负担。

问题在于他们将如何足够快地融入。首先，相当多的人将上海仅视为临时居住的落脚点，希望从这里找到通往世界上其他更适合他们吸收的地方的道路。然而，总会有一定数量的核心人群留在这里，由那些具有建设性作用的元素组成，如工业家、化学家、医生、教师、工匠和各种技术人员。最大的困难将是帮助他们过渡，直到他们逐渐适应城市的整体格局。

虽然不可否认，生活将变得压力稍大且竞争更加激烈，但移民们正在开辟各种活动，引入上海以前没有的、在某些技术和贸易商品方面的企业，这些领域与现有行业并不冲突。无论如何，这座城市拥有如此大的潜力，未来将在适当的职业中看到他们的身影。

希望的注脚

最有希望的一点是，当人们大规模聚集并和谐相处时，他们可以汇集技能和资源，创造出某种东西。对于这些难民来说，虽然被剥夺了手段，但在迫切需求的刺激下，他们的团结和协调必将产生成效并对城市有益，前提是他们的教友、朋友和支持者，在这里和世界各地，能首先维持他们的生存，使他们能够渡过难关，迎来必然到来的更好时期。

14080

SHANGHAI TIMES. MAY 24 1939
I 560
Jewish Influx
Being Studied
By Japanese
Emigrants May Conflict
With Japanese Or Aid
In Local Prosperity
MANCHOUKUO DOES NOT
WELCOME INFLUX
Immigration Can Only Be
Regulated At Source,
Says Spokesman
Japanese authorities in
Shanghai were studying the
problems arising out of the
growing influx here of Jewish
refugees from Europe, a Japan-
ese Embassy spokesman told
foreign newspaper correspond-
ents last evening when asked
to comment on a Japanese
press report alleging that the
local Japanese community was
aroused over the activities of
the refugees.
"It is difficult to generalize re-
garding this question," the spokes-
man said. Jewish commercial ac-
tivities in Shanghai could possibly
come into conflict with Japanese
interests, on the hand, while, on
the other, Jewish enterprise, by
increasing the prosperity of Shang-
hai, could benefit the Japanese.
He emphasized that the Jewish
immigration question was also being
discussed by various national com-
munities in Shanghai other than
Japanese, with the question of com-
petition between existing firms and
newly-established enterprises at-
tracting widespread attention.
The influx of European refugees,
he said, could only be regulated at
its source, principally by restrict-
ing the number of tickets sold to
persons bound for Shanghai.
The Japanese authorities, the
spokesman said, were not taking
the initiative in efforts to restrict
Jewish immigration to Shanghai
inasmuch as they considered the
question to be more within the
province of the Consular Body than
any individual Power.
Manchoukuo View
Manchoukuo, the spokesman con-
tinued, "does not welcome Jewish
mass immigration" but was not dis-
criminating against Jews because
of their race or creed.
"In keeping with its fundamental
policy of concord among the five
races which comprise Manchoukuo,"
the spokesman stated, the Hsinking
authorities were dealing with any
foreigner in the same manner.
Influx Feared
Jewish emigrants flocking into
the areas north of Soochow Creek
are becoming a serious problem
for the Japanese community, the
Shanghai "Mainichi" said on Mon-
day night.
Jewish "kingdoms" are being
formed near the Astor Hotel, in the
Hongkew sub-agency building of
the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank-
ing Corporation, and in Yangtzepoo
districts, the paper said.
It was possible, the journal stated,
that these emigrants from Europe
may encroach upon the rights and
interests of Japanese residents in
Hongkew because of their "peculiar
commercial ingenuity."
Their number already is 9,000 and
it was expected that it will increase
to 20,000 within this year, the daily
said.
（批：A refs'）
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1939年5月24日
I 560

日本研究
犹太人流
移民可能
与日本人冲突
或助长当地繁荣

满洲国不欢迎
大量流入

发言人称移民
只能在源头管制

昨晚，一位日本大使馆发言人在被要求就日本报纸关于当地日本社区因难民活动而感到不安的报道发表评论时，告诉外国报社记者，上海日本当局正在研究因欧洲犹太难民不断涌入上海而产生的问题。

“很难对这个问题进行概括，”该发言人说。一方面，犹太人在上海的商业活动可能与日本利益发生冲突；另一方面，犹太企业通过增加上海的繁荣，也可能使日本人受益。他强调，除了日本人之外，上海的其他各国侨民社区也在讨论犹太移民问题，现有公司与新成立企业之间的竞争问题引起了广泛关注。

他说，欧洲难民的涌入只能在其源头进行管制，主要是限制出售给前往上海人员的船票数量。

该发言人表示，日本当局并未主动采取措施限制犹太人移民上海，因为他们认为这个问题更多属于领事团的职权范围，而非任何一个单独国家的职权。

满洲国的观点

该发言人继续说道，满洲国“不欢迎犹太人大规模移民”，但并未因种族或信仰而歧视犹太人。

发言人称，“为了符合满洲国由五个民族组成的和谐基本政策”，新京当局对待任何外国人都采取相同的方式。

担忧涌入

上海《每日新闻》周一晚间称，涌入苏州河北岸地区的犹太移民正成为日本社区的一个严重问题。

该报称，在阿斯特饭店（Astor Hotel）附近、汇丰银行虹口代理处大楼以及杨树浦地区，正在形成犹太人的“王国”。

该报刊称，这些来自欧洲的移民可能因其“独特的商业才智”而侵犯虹口日本居民的权利和利益。

该日报称，他们的人数已达9,000人，预计今年内将增加到20,000人。
（批：A refs'）

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES,
MAY 9 1939
06871

Flow Of Refugees Into City
Creating Many Problems

1,500 More Expected Within Two Weeks; 450
Arrived On Sunday; Four Camps Now In
Existence; More Fu 's Are Needed

Not since the gloom following the Great War when Russian immigrants crowded the routes to China, has this country, especially Shanghai, experienced problems of immigration such as it is experiencing at the present time. The number of Jewish refugees that have arrived in Shanghai now total 8,800 and it appears that each boat arriving from Europe will increase this figure. On Sunday 450 came to Shanghai aboard the Lloyd Triestino's vessel Conte Rosso and three Italian ships expected to arrive within the next two weeks will deposit 1,500 more in Shanghai, bringing the total up to 10,300, while the end is not yet in sight.

Efforts To Help
Refugee Committees, which have done incomparable work since the start of the influx into Shanghai, are making feverish preparations to accommodate those already here and those due to arrive. No one is taking a pleasant view of the establishment of a European refugee centre in Shanghai, but it remains the only possible port which immigrants can enter since the majority cannot comply or fulfil the immigration requirements of other countries. The influx of such a friendly Jewish population into the city has already greatly loosened the purse-strings of Jewish and other financiers in aid of a worthy cause.

The majority of the German refugees from Berlin, Vienna, and Hamburg are men, mostly because they were sent away from the concentration camps and were forced to leave Germany. Many have their wives and children here, but many have not. Some were permitted to take money from the country and only a few have enough money on their person for the immediate necessities of life. When the deportation from Germany commenced, the refugees were allowed to take clothes and baggage with them but recent arrivals came with merely handbags, stating they were not permitted to bring their other property.

Four Camps Now
The International and Jewish Committees have now established four camps and a hospital in the city. No. 1 camp is located on Ward Road, No. 2 at Wayside, No. 3 in the Embankment Building and the recently created one on Chaoufoong Road. Most of the buildings were badly damaged but the refugees have repaired them and each day are making the camps more comfortable to live in. Bathrooms, sitting rooms and the like are being installed, while magazines, books, etc., are being donated to make life in the camps more pleasant. The refugees are all hoping to be able to leave the camps soon and already they are renting rooms in houses in which four to six people live.

Scarlet Fever Epidemic
As is always the case when numbers of people live close together in camps, diseases are quick to spread. There is a slight scarlet fever epidemic in the camps at the present time and all camps are closed under quarantine. Since the camps are under strict medical supervision, it is not believed that the fever actually started in the camps, but was brought in by outside persons. The number of scarlet fever cases is approximately 105, but all cases are being treated. The maintenance of health is the primary task of the committees. The Public Health Department of the Shanghai Municipal Council is co-operating with those in charge of camps and the situation is under control.

The Jewish refugees now have their own hospital on Whashing Road, which has about 40 beds. The doctors are all refugees and many of them were formerly among the finest in Germany, being chiefly surgeons of Berlin and Vienna hospitals. It is full at present, with 13 scarlet fever cases and the rest of the inmates suffering with various other diseases. Doctors, specialists and the medicine supply are sufficient.

Jewish School Suspended
To improve the situation for the refugees, the committee contemplated opening a Jewish school this week but the prevalence of the scarlet fever epidemic forced those in charge to abandon this project. Due to the fact that the summer will soon be here and revenue to operate the school being hardly sufficient, the school may not open until the autumn season.

The registration centre of the refugees is located at 190 Kiukiang Road, 2nd floor. Here each incoming refugee registers the most important particulars concerning himself and supplies a picture. He is required to have this registration card on his person while another card is kept on file in this office. This measure was instituted to assist in controlling and governing the refugees as also to assist the police.

In spite of the fact that the majority of the Jewish refugees are somewhat despondent and have no definite outlook for the future, the morale is high and their conduct has been very good. They are smartly dressed and clean, in spite of limited private facilities for many of them.

Additional funds are now needed by the committee to further maintain and improve local refugee institutions. Without definite sources of revenue it is extremely difficult for the committees to plan or materialize any project.

（批：Si / Jo P. ids: / D S Pult）
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，
1939年5月9日
06871

难民涌入市区
造成诸多问题

预计两周内还将有1,500人抵达；周日已有450人到达；现有四个营地；需要更多傅氏（Fu's）援助

自大战后俄罗斯移民挤满通往中国的路线所带来的阴霾以来，这个国家，尤其是上海，从未像现在这样面临如此严峻的移民问题。目前抵达上海的犹太难民总数已达8,800人，而且看来每一艘从欧洲驶来的船只都会使这一数字增加。周日，450名难民乘坐意大利劳埃德三隅公司（Lloyd Triestino）的“罗索伯爵号”（Conte Rosso）轮抵达上海，预计未来两周内抵达的三艘意大利船只将再送来1,500人，使总数达到10,300人，而尽头尚不可见。

援助努力
自难民涌入上海开始以来，各难民委员会开展了无与伦比的工作，目前正加紧准备，以安置已经在此以及即将抵达的难民。没有人乐见在上海建立一个欧洲难民中心，但这仍然是移民能够进入的唯一可能的港口，因为大多数人无法满足或履行其他国家的移民要求。如此友好的犹太人口涌入本市，已经极大地促使犹太裔及其他金融家慷慨解囊，资助这项崇高的事业。

来自柏林、维也纳和汉堡的德国难民大多是男性，这主要是因为他们被从集中营遣送出来，被迫离开德国。许多人的妻儿已在此处，但许多人并非如此。有些人获准携带资金出境，但只有少数人身上的钱足以应付眼前的生活必需品。当从德国的驱逐行动开始时，难民被允许携带衣物和行李，但最近抵达的人仅带着手提包，称他们不被允许携带其他财产。

现有四个营地
国际委员会和犹太委员会现已在本市建立了四个营地和一家医院。第一营地位于华德路（Ward Road），第二营地在韦赛德（Wayside），第三营地在堤岸大厦（Embankment Building），最近的一个位于兆丰路（Chaoufoong Road）。大多数建筑物受损严重，但难民们已对其进行修缮，并每天都在使营地更加适宜居住。浴室、休息室等设施正在安装中，同时杂志、书籍等物品也被捐赠出来，以使营地生活更加愉快。难民们都希望能尽快离开营地，目前他们已在一些容纳四至六人居住的房屋中租用房间。

猩红热疫情
正如人群在营地中密集居住时常见的那样，疾病迅速蔓延。目前营地内出现轻微的猩红热疫情，所有营地均因检疫而关闭。由于营地处于严格的医疗监督之下，人们认为发热病例并非起源于营地内部，而是由外部人员带入。猩红热病例数约为105例，但所有病例均在接受治疗。维持健康是委员会的首要任务。上海公共租界工部局公共卫生处正与营地负责人合作，局势已得到控制。

犹太难民目前在华盛路（Whashing Road）拥有自己的医院，设有约40张床位。医生均为难民，其中许多人曾是德国最优秀的医生，主要是柏林和维也纳医院的外科医生。目前医院已满员，收治了13名猩红热患者，其余住院者患有各种其他疾病。医生、专家及药品供应充足。

犹太学校停课
为改善难民的处境，委员会曾考虑本周开设一所犹太学校，但鉴于猩红热疫情流行，负责人被迫放弃此计划。由于夏季即将来临，且运营学校的资金几乎不足，该校可能要等到秋季才能开学。

难民登记中心位于九江路190号二楼。每位新到的难民需在此登记最重要的个人信息并提供照片。他必须随身携带此登记卡，另一份卡片则存档于该办公室。采取这一措施旨在协助管理和治理难民，同时也为警方提供协助。

尽管大多数犹太难民情绪有些低落，对未来没有明确的展望，但士气高昂，行为表现非常好。尽管许多人的私人设施有限，但他们衣着整洁干净。

委员会目前需要额外资金，以进一步维持和改善本地的难民机构。如果没有确定的收入来源，委员会极难规划或实现任何项目。

SHANGHAI TIMES,

MAY 4 1939

JEWS IN CHINA
In forwarding to this office a copy
of the first number of the "Gelbe Post,"
the publisher and editor, Mr. A. J.
Storfer, asked our opinion on the subject
of the settlement of Central European
Jews in South-West China. In his letter
he propounded the following questions:
(1) is it desirable that Jews, emigrated
from Central Europe, should settle in
South-West China; (2) are there only
certain categories ineligible for emigra-
tion to South-West China and which are
they; (3) what ought to happen if the
Chinese Government is moved to follow
up this plan and to realize it; (4) should
not the assistance of one or the other of
the leading corporations abroad and
locally be solicited for the furtherance of
this project; and (5) should emigrants be
brought first to Shanghai and then sent
to South-West China or should steps be
taken to send them direct to South-West
China? In reply to these questions, we
fear that we must declare that in our
opinion the settlement of any large number
of European Jews in South-West China is
an impracticable proposition. The province
of Yunnan, which has been particularly
mentioned in this connection, still exhibits
primitive conditions and obviously could
not support any large number of foreign-
ers whose standard of living is so far
superior to that of the Chinese. While
individual Jews or other foreigners might
be able to secure posts of some sort in
the interior it is only in large Treaty
ports like Shanghai and Tientsin that
anything like a foreign colony can
permanently sustain itself. We fear that
any foreign colony established in the
interior of China must soon become an
economic failure and that those of its
members who survived would be absorbed
by the surrounding Chinese masses. For
the Jews, there is the warning of Kai-
feng, where the ancient Jewish community
gradually died out or became absorbed
in the Chinese population.

D. C. P. K.
S. I. / R

1939年5月4日

在华犹太人

《黄色邮报》（Gelbe Post）第一期副本送至本办事处时，出版人兼编辑A. J. Storfer先生征求我们就中欧犹太人在中国西南定居问题的意见。他在信中提出了以下问题：(1) 从中欧移民出来的犹太人定居在中国西南是否可取；(2) 是否只有某些类别的人不适合移民到中国西南，具体是哪些类别；(3) 如果中国政府被推动跟进并实施此计划，应当发生什么情况；(4) 是否应寻求国外或当地一家或多家主要公司的协助以促进该项目；以及 (5) 应先将移民带至上海，然后再送往中国西南，还是应采取步骤直接将他们送往中国西南？针对这些问题，我们恐怕必须声明，在我们看来，让大量欧洲犹太人在中国西南定居是一个不切实际的提议。在此背景下被特别提及的云南省，仍然呈现出原始状态，显然无法支撑大量生活水平远高于中国人的外国人。虽然个别犹太人或其他外国人可能能够在内地谋得某种职位，但只有在像上海和天津这样的大型通商口岸，外国侨民群体才能永久维持下去。我们担心，在中国内地建立的任何外国侨民群体很快就会在经济上失败，而那些幸存的成员将被周围的广大中国民众所同化。对于犹太人而言，开封就是一个警示，那里的古老犹太社区逐渐消亡或被同化进中国人口中。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 5 1939
“Code Of Conduct” For Jewish
Refugees In England
A “code of conduct” for Jewish refugees in England has been drawn up by the Board of Deputies of British Jews. In return for British hospitality, the code requests the refugees to “carry out to your utmost the following lines of conduct. Regard them as duties to which you are in honour bound.” The code instructs them to:
1.—Spend your spare time immediately in learning the English language and its correct pronunciation.
2.—Refrain from speaking German in the streets and public places. Do not read German newspapers in public.
3.—Do not join any political organization or take part in any political activities.
4.—Do not criticize Government regulations or the way things are done over here.
5.—Do not make yourself conspicuous by speaking loudly, nor by your manner of dress. The Englishmen greatly dislike ostentation.
6.—Try to observe and follow the manners and customs and habits of this country in social and business relations.
7.—Above all, realize that the Jewish community is relying on you to uphold in this country the highest Jewish qualities, to maintain dignity and to help and serve others.
“It must not be said that the refugees are taking work away from British workers,” the code continues. You must not accept any employment, paid or unpaid, or engage in any business or profession without written permission from the aliens department of the Home Office—nor may you take permitted work at a wage less than the customary wage.
“The Home Office will always give consideration to the cases of business and professional men who can bring to this country special knowledge and skill not already here.”

英国犹太难民的“行为准则”

英国犹太人代表委员会制定了在英国犹太难民的“行为准则”。作为对英国款待的回报，该准则要求难民“尽最大努力执行以下行为准则。将其视为您荣誉所系的责任。”该准则指示他们：
1.—立即利用空闲时间学习英语及其正确发音。
2.—避免在街道和公共场所讲德语。不要在公共场合阅读德文报纸。
3.—不要加入任何政治组织或参与任何政治活动。
4.—不要批评政府法规或这里的行事方式。
5.—不要因大声说话或穿着打扮而引人注目。英国人非常不喜欢炫耀。
6.—在社交和商业关系中，努力观察并遵循本国的礼仪、习俗和习惯。
7.—最重要的是，要认识到犹太社区依靠你们在这个国家维护最高的犹太品质，保持尊严，并帮助和服务他人。
“绝不能说难民抢走了英国工人的工作，”准则继续说道，“未经内政部外籍人士部门书面许可，你们不得接受任何有偿或无偿的工作，或从事任何商业或职业活动——也不得以低于 customary wage（常规工资）的工资从事获准的工作。”
“内政部将始终考虑那些能为本国带来此处尚未具备的特殊知识和技能的商界及专业人士的案例。”

FEB 12 1939
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. C. REGISTRY No. S. 11. D. 44249）

Jewish Refugees May Be Given
An Island Off Singapore

There is a possibility that at some future date, permission may be sought to use an island off Singapore as a haven for Jewish refugees from Germany should they ever be caught between Malaya and Shanghai.

This is envisaged in the event of Shanghai being suddenly closed to refugees owing to the huge numbers which are now pouring in.

This experiment has already been tried at Manila, and the Malaya "Tribune" has it on good authority that it is a success.

The question of such colonisation is fraught with difficulty, and in the choice of people who would be the pioneers of such a colony there must be careful discrimination.

Engineers, doctors and electricians would have to be among those who first set foot on land destined to be the future home of a new colony and only people capable of organization and development would be selected.

It is not likely that colonization of islands about Singapore will take place in the near future because at the present moment there is no necessity for such a step.

There are many Jewish refugees in Singapore who are being assisted by the Jewish Relief Committee, and among them are skilled doctors, engineers, mechanics and caterers.

The suggestion that doctors would be of use in Singapore as practitioners is affected by the fact that any doctors practising in Singapore must have British certificates.

The Jewish Refugee doctors do not possess these, but the Relief Committee holds out hopes of getting these doctors placed in institutes of research on a temporary basis. If this is possible it will help to deal with the problem.

犹太难民或可获得新加坡附近的一个岛屿

未来有可能寻求许可，使用新加坡附近的一个岛屿作为来自德国的犹太难民的避难所，以防他们被困在马来亚和上海之间。

这是考虑到由于目前涌入的人数巨大，上海可能突然对难民关闭的情况。

马尼拉已经尝试过这种实验，据马来亚《论坛报》（Tribune）从可靠消息源获悉，此举取得了成功。

此类殖民化问题困难重重，在选择将成为此类殖民地先驱的人员时必须仔细甄别。

工程师、医生和电工必须属于首批踏上这片注定成为新殖民地未来家园的土地的人，且只应选择具备组织和发展能力的人。

新加坡周边岛屿的殖民化不太可能在近期发生，因为目前没有必要采取此类步骤。

新加坡有许多犹太难民正得到犹太救济委员会的援助，其中包括技术娴熟的医生、工程师、机械师和餐饮供应商。

关于医生在新加坡作为执业医师会有用处的建议，受到这样一个事实的影响：即任何在新加坡执业的医生都必须持有英国证书。

犹太难民医生不具备这些证书，但救济委员会表示有望将这些医生暂时安置在研究机构中。如果这成为可能，将有助于解决这一问题。

mediately with their home governments in the matter, pointing out that the labour and employment problem in Shanghai is already sufficiently acute and that matters will not be helped by the arrival of several hundred more foreign unemployed (in certain cases, this has already been done).

It is suggested that the home governments draw the attention of the emigres to the undesirability of Shanghai as a place of refuge and that the governments endeavour to persuade them not to come here, with the help of such mediums as posters and circulars to travel and shipping agencies.

Beyond this, however, the Consular Body cannot see what else it is in a position to do, it is learnt. Solution of the problem is not a simple one, for it bristles with all sorts of minor yet none the less grave difficulties.

Various Problems

For instance, in the case of Jewish refugees from Germany, these seldom board a vessel in a German port for Shanghai. They go on board in, say, a French or Italian port. The German Government is glad to see them cross the frontier and leave the country, there its responsibility for them ends.

On the other hand, the French and Italian governments have not evinced any desire to house the refugees and are, therefore, equally glad to see them board a steamer and leave for other parts of the world—which for many for them, those without passports, can only mean Shanghai.

There is also the point of view of the shipping companies concerned. Looking at the problem objectively, it is not for them to inquire into the financial history of intending passengers; providing the latter pay the fare (and, what is more, are being encouraged to leave the country) the shipping company is fully entitled to accept them as ordinary, bona fide passengers, which is what they are. Their reasons for wishing to leave Europe are not the concern of the shipping company.

On the other hand, should pressure be brought to bear upon the shipping companies by certain governments as a result of the pleas of the Consular Body and the Shanghai Municipal Council, there is nothing to prevent the emigres from combining and chartering one or more ships for their exclusive use from any one of hundreds of companies all over the world.

Visas Granted

Chinese consulates in Europe are granting visas to all those applying with their passports for permission to come to Shanghai; this, it was pointed out to "The Shanghai Sunday Times" yesterday, was fully in accordance with the terms of the agreements between China and the various Powers whereby Shanghai became a treaty port.

No request is being addressed to the Chinese Government by the Council or the Consular Body, it is understood, asking it to instruct its consulates not to issue such visas, a step which could be taken if the Consular Body and the Council could persuade the Government that, in view of prevailing conditions here, the refugees could be classed as "undesirables," without any reflections on their characters.

The reason why no such request is being made is obvious. There is no Chinese passport bureau in Shanghai now, due to the hostilities, and entrance into Shanghai can be secured without visa and without passport. It might seem ironic to some that the ill wind of war which has hit Shanghai should prove to be the good wind of refuge to hundreds who otherwise would be faced with the problem of being practically forced to leave their own country, only to find the doors of every other country closed against all but a handful.

At present, as revealed in "The Shanghai Times" at the end of last month, the situation is a grave one. By the end of March, Jewish refugees here are expected to number over 4,000; a very large proportion will be practically destitute and will have to be looked after, and all will be unemployed.

In about a fortnight, if not sooner, the local Jewish relief organizations which have been handling the matter will find themselves without funds and with nearly 3,000 unfortunate people on their hands. At the moment, they have absolutely no prospects of raising the necessary money, the response from home bodies to appeals for help having been practically negligible. Shanghai itself will have to do something for these people.

Suggested Remedy

A suggestion was made in one quarter yesterday that the best solution out of the present difficulty might be the establishment of a fully-contained camp somewhat on the lines of the new camp for 10,000 Chinese refugees, which has just been opened off Tunsin Road.

A great deal of the present expenditure caused by having the refugees living in various parts of the city would be done away with in such camp owing to the centralization of kitchens, dormitories, laundries, clinics, offices and so on.

Such a camp would also solve the question of finding work for the people and would also calm the fears of those who are scared lest the emigres desperately accept positions at starvation rates and thus undercut the present market for employment.

Work Provided

The refugees would be given work to do in the camp, as is done in the Chinese camps, such work ranging all the way from weaving cloth and making up suits of clothing for members of the community to "taking in each other's washing."

Occasionally, where an opportunity offered, Sir Victor Sassoon's rehabilitation fund could be used to assist refugees in setting up for themselves, enabling them to leave the camp and take their places as fully supporting and self-respecting members of the international community of Shanghai.

Some attempt along these lines is already being made by the Committee for the Assistance of European Jewish Emigres, but the lack of funds and other resources is making the task an almost insurmountable one.

The Tunsin Road camp cost about $90,000 to put into working order, a sum which, curiously enough, is almost the same as the present monthly cost of supporting the Jewish emigres. Of this sum, $25,000 was donated by the Shanghai Municipal Council; $25,000 by the Shanghai Refugee Relief Association; and the remaining $40,000 was received in the shape of donations.
pages.zh:
指出上海的劳工和就业问题已经足够严峻，再有数百名外国失业者到来无助于事态改善（在某些情况下，此举已经完成）。

建议本国政府提请移民注意，上海作为避难地并不适宜，并借助海报和发给旅行及航运代理机构的通函等手段，努力说服他们不要前来此地。

然而，除此之外，据悉领事团看不出还能做些什么。解决这一问题并非易事，因为它充满了各种虽小却同样严重的困难。

各种问题

例如，就来自德国的犹太难民而言，他们很少在德国港口登船前往上海。他们通常在法国或意大利港口登船。德国政府乐于看到他们跨越边境离开该国，至此，德国政府对他们的责任即告终止。

另一方面，法国和意大利政府并未表现出收容难民的意愿，因此也同样乐于看到他们登上轮船前往世界其他地区——对于许多人，特别是那些没有护照的人来说，这意味着只能去上海。

还有相关轮船公司的角度。客观地看这个问题，调查潜在乘客的财务历史并非他们的职责；只要后者支付船费（而且，更重要的是，他们正被鼓励离开该国），轮船公司完全有权将他们作为普通的、善意的乘客接受，事实也确实如此。他们希望离开欧洲的原因不是轮船公司需要关心的事。

另一方面，如果由于领事团和上海公共租界工部局的呼吁，某些政府对轮船公司施加压力，这并不能阻止移民联合起来，从全球数百家轮船公司中的任何一家包租一艘或多艘船只供其专用。

签发签证

欧洲的中国领事馆正在向所有持护照申请许可来上海的人签发签证；昨天有人向《上海星期泰晤士报》指出，这完全符合中国与列强之间使上海成为通商口岸的各项协定条款。

据了解，工部局或领事团均未向中国政府提出请求，要求其指示各领事馆停止签发此类签证。如果领事团和工部局能够说服中国政府，鉴于上海目前的状况，可以将难民归类为“不受欢迎的人”，而这并不涉及对其品格的非议，那么本可以采取这一步骤。

未提出此类请求的原因显而易见。由于战事，上海目前没有中国护照签发机构，进入上海无需签证和护照。对一些人来说，这似乎具有讽刺意味：袭击上海的战争恶风，竟成了数百人的避难顺风，否则他们将面临几乎被迫离开自己国家的问题，却发现除少数几个国家外，其他所有国家的大门都对他们关闭。

目前，正如上月底《字林西报》所披露的那样，局势严峻。预计到3月底，在沪犹太难民人数将超过4,000人；其中很大一部分人将几乎一无所有，需要得到照顾，且所有人都处于失业状态。

大约两周后，如果不更早的话，一直处理此事的当地犹太救济组织将会发现自身资金耗尽，而手头仍有近3,000名不幸者。目前，他们绝对没有筹集到必要资金的希望，国内机构对援助呼吁的反应几乎微乎其微。上海本身必须为这些人做点什么。

建议的补救措施

昨天有一方提出建议，摆脱当前困境的最佳解决方案可能是建立一个完全封闭的营地，其模式类似于刚刚在敦信路（Tunsin Road）附近开设的可容纳10,000名中国难民的新营地。

由于厨房、宿舍、洗衣房、诊所、办公室等的集中化管理，这种营地可以消除因难民散居在城市各处而产生的大部分当前开支。

这样的营地还将解决为人们寻找工作的问题，并平息那些担心移民绝望地接受极低工资从而压低当前就业市场的人的恐惧。

提供工作

难民将在营地里获得工作机会，就像在中国难民营里所做的那样，这些工作范围广泛，从为社区成员织布和制作服装，到“互相代洗衣服”。

偶尔，如果有机会，维克多·沙逊爵士（Sir Victor Sassoon）的复兴基金可用于帮助难民自立，使他们能够离开营地，成为上海国际社会中完全自给自足且自尊的成员。

欧洲犹太移民援助委员会已经在沿袭这些思路进行一些尝试，但缺乏资金和其他资源使得这项任务几乎难以克服。

敦信路营地投入运作花费了约9万美元，奇怪的是，这笔金额几乎与支持犹太移民目前的月度费用相同。在这笔款项中，上海公共租界工部局捐赠了25,000美元；上海难民救济协会捐赠了25,000美元；其余40,000美元以捐款形式收到。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
JAN. 29 1939

Jewish Refugees From
Europe To Number Some
4,000 By End Of March

Conte Biancamano Sails From Naples With About
1,000 Emigres On Board; Conte Verde Due
In Port To-day With Another 400

RESOURCES OF LOCAL COMMITTEES
BEING STRAINED TO UTMOST

By the end of March, Jewish refugees from Europe living
in Shanghai are expected to number over 4,000. The Lloyd
Triestino liner Conte Verde is arriving in Shanghai to-day
with some 400 Jewish emigrés on board, while word was
received from Rome yesterday to the effect that 1,000 Jews,
mostly of German origin, sailed from Naples in the s.s. Conte
Biancamano on Friday, bound for Shanghai. They are due to
arrive here about February 22.
In addition to these two shiploads, two Hamburg-America
Line vessels are reported to have been specially chartered at
Hamburg to transport groups of
Jewish refugees from Germany to
Shanghai. While most of these re-
fugees will probably remain in
Shanghai to swell the present emigre
colony of 2,000, a few will sail for
Dairen, as about 300 have already
obtained permission from the port
authorities to settle there.
A group of 10 emigres were
landed last Friday from the Messa-
geries Maritimes motor liner Felix
Roussel, while another 100, com-
prising mostly refugees from Ger-
many, arrived yesterday in the
Norddeutscher Lloyd's Gneisenau.
These two groups have already
been given temporary places to live
in by the relief committees.

Committee Meets
At Mr. M. Speelman's home last
evening, members of the refugee
relief committee held another
meeting to discuss their problems.
Local assistance, it was reported,
has been slightly more favourable
during the past week, and several
small contributions which have
been received, besides furniture
and articles used for general pur-
poses, have made relief conditions
take on a more hopeful aspect.
As reported in "The Shanghai
Times" about a week ago, the
Shanghai Committee for the Assist-
ance of European Jewish Emigres
has already started to face an ex-
tremely serious situation owing to
a lack of sufficient funds to main-
tain the present community. The
arrival of another 2,000 will make
it even harder, as so far only about
20 per cent. of the refugees arriv-
ing here have been in a position to
provide for themselves, owing to
the stringent regulations in Ger-
many governing the export of per-
sonal monies and property.
A few donations have been re-
ceived, a sum of $6,000 from Singa-
pore and another $3,000 from Hong-
kong, while Sir Victor Sassoon,
who is at present in London, has
contributed $150,000 to a special re-
habilitation fund which aims at
providing refugees with assistance

《字林西报》。
1939年1月29日

来自欧洲的犹太难民
至三月底人数将达约4,000人

“比安卡马诺伯爵”号从那不勒斯启航，载有约1,000名移民；“绿伯爵”号今日抵港，另载400人

地方委员会的资源已紧绷至极限

预计到三月底，居住在上海的来自欧洲的犹太难民人数将超过4,000人。意大利劳埃德特里奥斯蒂诺公司（Lloyd Triestino）的“绿伯爵”号（Conte Verde）轮船今日抵达上海，船上载有约400名犹太移民；而昨日从罗马收到的消息指出，1,000名犹太人（大多为德国籍）已于周五从那不勒斯乘坐“比安卡马诺伯爵”号（s.s. Conte Biancamano）轮船启程，驶往上海。他们预计将于2月22日左右抵达此地。
除了这两批船运难民外，据报道，汉堡-美洲航运公司（Hamburg-America Line）的两艘船只已在汉堡被特别包租，用于运送成群的犹太难民从德国前往上海。虽然这些难民中的大多数人可能会留在上海，使目前的2,000名移民群体进一步扩大，但少数人将乘船前往大连，因为已有约300人获得了港口当局在那里定居的许可。
上周五，有一组10名移民从法国邮船公司（Messageries Maritimes）的机动邮轮“费利克斯·鲁塞尔”号（Felix Roussel）登陆，而另一组100人（主要由来自德国的难民组成）于昨日乘坐北德意志劳埃德公司（Norddeutscher Lloyd）的“格奈森瑙”号（Gneisenau）抵达。救济委员会已为这两组人提供了临时住所。

委员会召开会议
昨晚，在M. Speelman先生家中，难民救济委员会成员举行了另一次会议，讨论他们面临的问题。据报告，在过去的一周里，本地的援助情况略有好转，收到的一些小额捐款，以及家具和一般用途的物品，使得救济状况呈现出更为乐观的前景。
正如《字林西报》约一周前所报道的那样，上海援助欧洲犹太移民委员会（Shanghai Committee for the Assistance of European Jewish Emigres）由于缺乏维持现有社区所需的足够资金，已经开始面临极其严峻的局势。另外2,000人的到来将使情况更加困难，因为迄今为止，抵达此地的难民中只有约20%有能力自给自足，这是由于德国对个人资金和财产出口有着严格的规定。
已收到少量捐款，其中来自新加坡的6,000美元和来自香港的3,000美元，而目前身在伦敦的维克多·沙逊爵士（Sir Victor Sassoon）已向一个特别复兴基金捐赠了150,000美元，该基金旨在为难民在上海各类商业活动中提供职业方面的援助

in their professional capacities in
various businesses in Shanghai.
So far, only a bare handful of the
80 per cent., on the local refugees'
committees' hands have been able
to start contributing towards their
own upkeep.
Positions Found
A few doctors have been placed
with missionaries; several dentists
have gone into partnership and
opened a mutual office which they
share in two-hour periods during
the day; some newspapermen have
combined to bring out the "Ossia-
tischer Rundschau," which might
best be translated as the "Far East-
ern Weekly Mirror," and which is
specially designed to cater to the
news needs of the refugees here;
while another party of about 20
are combining to form a trucking
company. Several tailors and a
restaurateur have found positions.
also a night club manager and
several musicians, the latter includ-
ing Mr. E. Winkler, who made his
Shanghai debut with municipal or-
chestra a few weeks back.
In view of the refugee commit-
tee's policy in its Employment
Bureau of "hastening slowly,"
however, a large majority are still
unable to even partially fend for
themselves. The Employment
Bureau, from the start, was alive to
the possibility that rumours would
soon be flying around to the effect
that the refugees would undermine
local employment resources by
offering cheap labour.
The Bureau, as pointed out by
"The Shanghai Times" before, has
done all it can to prevent more re-
fugees from coming out to Shang-
hai, as it recognizes the fact that
Shanghai is in no position to absorb
these refugees at the moment. Care
has been taken to see that capital
will only be advanced to enable
businesses to be started where a
definite opening exists and also to
see that where refugees are given
employment they are merely filling
vacancies and are not displacing
any other employees.
pages.zh:
到目前为止，在当地难民委员会负责的80%的难民中，只有极少数人能够开始为自己的生活费用做出贡献。

找到职位
几名医生已被安置在传教士处工作；几名牙医合伙开设了一间共同诊所，他们在白天分两小时轮流使用；一些新闻工作者联合创办了《Ossiatischer Rundschau》，最好翻译为《远东周刊镜鉴》，专门满足此地难民的新闻需求；而另一群约20人正联合组建一家卡车运输公司。几名裁缝和一名餐馆经营者也找到了职位，还有一名夜总会经理和几名音乐家，后者包括E. Winkler先生，他几周前刚随工部局管弦乐队在上海首次亮相。
然而，鉴于难民委员会就业局采取“欲速则不达”（hastening slowly）的政策，绝大多数人仍然无法甚至部分地自食其力。就业局从一开始就意识到，谣言很快就会流传开来，称难民将通过提供廉价劳动力来破坏当地的就业资源。
正如《字林西报》此前指出的那样，该局已尽其所能防止更多难民前来上海，因为它认识到上海目前无力吸收这些难民。当局已谨慎行事，确保只提供启动资金用于在有明确市场空缺的地方开展业务，并确保难民受雇时只是填补空缺，而不是取代其他雇员。

pages.en:
Shanghai's Reaction
Shanghai's reaction to the mass
arrival of these refugees has been
somewhat mixed. This international
city's reputation of being a place
of refuge is a matter of pride to
those who have grown up with it,
who have seen the Russian colony
—refugees and emigres from a
country in the turmoil of revolution
—gradually become a part of the
life of Shanghai and a hard-working
section of its community which has
contributed more than its fair share
to the artistic life of the city as a
whole; and who have seen the
hundreds of thousands of Chinese
who, on many occasions in the past
two decades, have clamoured at the
gates for sanctuary.
But, as is pointed out, Shanghai
at the moment, with part of its ter-
ritory still beyond its control, and
with its internal population still
tremendously swelled by refugees
from the Sino-Japanese hostilities,
is in no position to handle another
large body of refugees.
According to the three committees
in charge of the problem—the Relief
Society for German-Austrian Jews,
the International Committee for
Granting Relief to European
Refugees, and the co-ordinating
organization headed by Mr. M.
Speelman, the Committee for the
Assistance of Jewish Refugees—a
sum of $90,000 is required each
month to support the present Euro-
pean refugee community of 2,000 or
so, which seems to imply that at
the end of March no less than
$180,000 will have to be found.
These committees fully realise
that Shanghai is not able to bear
such a burden at the present time
and are carrying on as best they
can in the hope that charitable or-
ganizations in the United States and
in England will be able to come to
their assistance in the near future.
Another Point Of View
On the other hand, in view of
the fact that immigration of Jewish
and part-Jewish populations from
the Reich is more than encouraged,
there is a great deal of sympathy
shown in Shanghai towards these
unfortunate people.
"You might say it was a case of
jumping out of the fire into the
frying-pan!" one local resident of
many years standing commented to
a representative of "The Shanghai
Sunday Times." Most of these
refugees, he pointed out, were
pages.zh:
上海的反应
上海对这些难民大规模抵达的反应有些复杂。这座国际城市作为避难所的声誉，是那些与之共同成长的人们的骄傲，他们见证了俄罗斯侨民——来自革命动荡国家的难民和移民——逐渐融入上海的生活，成为社区中勤劳的一部分，为整个城市的艺术生活做出了超出其份额的贡献；他们也见证了过去二十年中，成千上万的中国人多次在门口 clamoured（恳求/喧哗）寻求庇护。
但是，正如所指出的那样，上海目前部分领土仍不在其控制之下，且内部人口因中日敌对行动产生的难民而大幅膨胀，因此无力应对另一大批难民。
根据负责处理此问题的三个委员会——德奥犹太救济协会（Relief Society for German-Austrian Jews）、欧洲难民国际救济委员会（International Committee for Granting Relief to European Refugees）以及由M. Speelman先生领导的协调组织“援助犹太难民委员会”（Committee for the Assistance of Jewish Refugees）——每月需要90,000美元来维持目前约2,000人的欧洲难民社区，这似乎意味着到三月底将不得不筹集至少180,000美元。
这些委员会充分认识到上海目前无法承受如此沉重的负担，并正在尽最大努力维持，希望美国和英国的慈善组织能在不久的将来提供援助。

另一种观点
另一方面，鉴于来自纳粹德国的犹太人和半犹太人人口的移民不仅被允许而且受到鼓励，上海对这些不幸的人表现出了极大的同情。
“你可以说这是‘跳出火坑，又入油锅’！”一位在当地居住多年的居民对《上海星期泰晤士报》（The Shanghai Sunday Times）的代表评论道。他指出，这些难民中的大多数是

pages.en:
in business or professions and
it must have been very hard
for them to give home and
everything up and travel across
the world to a strange city, whose
language most of them could not
speak, and where they knew they
would prove a burden on a com-
munity already carrying more than
its fair share of such humanitarian
work.

Indeed, most of them would
probably prefer to go anywhere but
to Shanghai. But most of the coun-
tries of the world had closed their
doors to all but an infinitesimal
number of refugees and Shanghai
might almost take pride in the fact
that, through a strange quirk, it was
now practically the only place in
the world where these refugees
could seek sanctuary.

He himself felt that since the
majority of the refugees would, in
better times, be a definite asset to
Shanghai that, over-taxed as its
resources were, Shanghai's foreign
population could, if it tried, meet
the demand.

"Most of us, I am sure, could
afford to devote $5 a month to this
humanitarian work," he said, "and
that should be enough to help the
committees until more appropriate
assistance comes from organizations
abroad."

In conclusion, he compared the
present plight of the European re-
fugees with that of the foreign
refugees from Shanghai who in
August and September, 1937, poured
into Hongkong and Manila, strongly
taxing the efforts of the authorities
there to meet the demand. No sug-
gestion that no more refugees could
be taken was made at that time by
either port, he said.

"Centres" Formed

Meanwhile, the local committees
are carrying on as best they can.
Newcomers are rapidly found
shelter, either in private houses or
in rooms in private houses rented
by the committees, or else in
"centres" such as the Embankment
Building or the former premises of
the old Customs training school in
Ward Road, opposite the gaol, where
1,200 are to be accommodated when
the building will be ready for
occupation early next week.

The monetary assistance required
of Shanghai is a temporary measure,
as a big proportion of the money
goes to the upkeep of refugees tem-
porarily housed in various boarding
houses. In the near future, it is
hoped, fairly large blocks of build-
ings in the Hongkew and Wayside
areas will be taken over, with
arrangements for a centralized
system of distributing food. This
will lower present costs consider-
ably.

In the interim, however, the task
of the refugee committees is a
difficult one and is not being made
any easier by fresh influxes of
emigres. The Consular Body, at the
request of the Shanghai Municipal
Council, is looking into the ques-
tion with a view to seeing what
can be done to, temporarily at least,
stop further refugees from coming
to Shanghai. So far, however, it
has not been able to arrive at any
definite conclusions in the matter.
pages.zh:
从事商业或专业工作的人，对他们来说，放弃家园和一切，跨越世界来到一个陌生的城市一定非常艰难，他们中大多数人不会说这里的语言，而且他们知道自己将成为一个已经承担了过多此类人道主义工作的社区的负担。

的确，他们中的大多数人可能宁愿去任何地方也不愿来上海。但是，世界上大多数国家的大门只对极少量的难民开放，上海几乎可以自豪地表示，由于一种奇怪的巧合，这里现在几乎是世界上难民唯一可以寻求庇护的地方。

他本人认为，既然大多数难民在更好的时期肯定会对上海有所贡献，那么尽管资源过度紧张，上海的外国人口如果努力的话，是可以满足这一需求的。

“我相信，我们大多数人每月拿出5美元用于这项人道主义工作是负担得起的，”他说，“这应该足以帮助委员会，直到国外组织提供更适当的援助。”

最后，他将欧洲难民目前的困境与1937年8月和9月从上海涌入香港和马尼拉的外国难民的处境进行了比较，当时那里的当局为满足需求付出了巨大的努力。他说，当时这两个港口都没有提出不能再接收难民的建议。

形成“中心”

与此同时，地方委员会正在尽最大努力维持运作。新来者很快就被安排了住所，要么住在私人住宅里，要么住在委员会租用的私人住宅房间里，或者住在诸如外滩大楼（Embankment Building）或位于华德路（Ward Road）、监狱对面的旧海关训练学校旧址等“中心”。当该建筑在下周初准备好入住时，将容纳1,200人。

上海所需的金钱援助是一项临时措施，因为大部分资金用于维持暂时寄宿在各种寄宿公寓中的难民的生活。希望在不久的将来，虹口（Hongkew）和越界筑路区（Wayside areas）的大片建筑群将被接管，并安排集中分发食物的系统。这将大大降低目前的成本。

然而，在此期间，难民委员会的任务十分艰巨，新移民的不断涌入使任务变得更加困难。应上海公共租界工部局的要求，领事团正在调查此事，以期看看能做些什么，至少在暂时阻止更多难民前来上海。然而，到目前为止，在此事上尚未得出任何明确的结论。

《上海泰晤士报》，
1939年1月15日

援助欧洲移民委员会
急需帮助

目前救济团体手中的资金
几乎微不足道；今日抵达的
250人加剧了忧虑

知情人士表示困难
属暂时性质

昨日，一位权威人士向《上海星期泰晤士报》记者透露，由于缺乏足够资金来维持对1,500多名来自德国和奥地利的难民的救助工作，本地欧洲犹太移民援助委员会目前正面临极其严峻的局势。令这一焦虑雪上加霜的是，今天又有两批人员抵达上海，总人数近250人。据悉，这些人中约80%无法自给自足，将不得不依赖本地救济机构所能提供的帮助。尽管本市参与解决欧洲移民救济问题的欧洲籍成员以及各移民福利机构在发出紧急呼吁寻求快速援助后，局面显得较为乐观——特别是确认了维克多·沙逊爵士（Sir Victor Sassoon）拨款15万美元用于安置的消息——但人们指出，应当清楚认识到这笔巨额拨款的性质。维克多爵士的捐款专门用于资助一个特定基金，该基金旨在帮助来此定居并开展业务的移民。有人强调，设立该基金的唯一目的是避免上海出现进一步的经济或失业问题。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
JAN 1 4 1939

Sassoon Aids
Emigres With
$150,000 Sum

Money Earmarked For
Rehabilitation Of
Refugees Here

GENERAL FUND IS
IN SORRY WAY

Expected Arrival Here
To-morrow Of 300
More Persons

From a report received In
Shanghai yesterday, it was
established that Sir Victor
Sassoon, local utilities magnate
who is at present staying in
London, has contributed the
sum of $150,000 to the Com-
mittee in charge here of the
rehabilitation fund for Euro-
pean-Jewish emigres.

According to its designation, the
large sum of money has been ear-
marked for the special rehabilita-
tion fund which was created a
short while ago by Sir Elly
Kadoorie, K.B.E., and Messrs. M.
Speelman (the Chairman of this
special group), Ellis Hayim, E.
Kelen (former Austrian consul
here), R. M. Joseph and K. M.
Joseph, and aiming at providing
assistance in their professional
capacities to the European-Jewish
refugees in various businesses here.

Already, it may be noted, the
committee has helped to establish
doctors, tailors, and, in one in-
stance, even a restaurateur. The
money in this fund, however, was
running short, and the special
grant by Sir Victor Sassoon, which
was urgently cabled here, has
brought timely aid to the group's
aim.

It was earlier explained by the
committee that rumours prevailing
locally regarding dismissal of work-
ers to make place for the emigres
were totally unfounded. The com-
mittee plans only to give positions
to emigres where vacancies occur,
it was emphasized.

The general fund which provides
for the maintenance of nearly 1,500
emigres, and for which a monthly
sum of nearly $90,000 is required
at present, is in a sorry position
owing to a lack of sufficient funds
for relief distribution.

While it has been pointed out
that the people in Shanghai can-
not at the present time afford to
donate $90,000 monthly, hope was
asserted that aid would be forth-
coming in this direction from
charitable organizations in the
United States and in England,
within the near future.

According to an informed report
made here yesterday, the s.s. San-
sho, a Japanese coastal freighter,
sailed from Hongkong yesterday
morning and is expected to arrive
in Shanghai to-morrow afternoon,
bringing about 50 emigres who
trans-shipped at the colony from
a European vessel.

In addition to this group about
200 more refugees are expected to
land here to-morrow in the Lloyd
Triestino liner Victoria, when she
docks at the Shanghai and Hongkew
Wharf.

An interesting feature of the
batch coming here on the Italian
liner, are 20 persons in the same
group who are proceeding to Dai-
ren. It is understood that a total
of nearly 300 emigres have obtain-
ed permission from the port
authorities at Dairen to settle there.

《上海泰晤士报》，
1939年1月14日

沙逊资助
移民15万美元

款项指定用于
此地难民的
安置工作

普通基金
状况堪忧

预计明日将有
另外300人
抵达此地

根据昨日在上海收到的一份报告，证实目前旅居伦敦的本地公用事业巨头维克多·沙逊爵士已向负责管理欧洲犹太移民安置基金的本地委员会捐赠了15万美元。

根据指定用途，这笔巨款已划拨给不久前由埃利·嘉道理爵士（Sir Elly Kadoorie, K.B.E.）、M. 斯皮尔曼先生（该特别小组主席）、埃利斯·哈伊姆（Ellis Hayim）、E. 凯伦（E. Kelen，前奥地利驻沪领事）、R. M. 约瑟夫（R. M. Joseph）和 K. M. 约瑟夫（K. M. Joseph）创立的特别安置基金，旨在从职业能力方面为在此从事各类行业的欧洲犹太难民提供援助。

值得注意的是，该委员会已协助安置了医生、裁缝，甚至在某一案例中协助安置了一位餐馆老板。然而，该基金的资金此前已告短缺，维克多·沙逊爵士通过电报紧急汇来的特别拨款为该团体的目标提供了及时援助。

委员会早前解释说，本地流传的关于雇主解雇现有员工以为移民腾出职位的谣言毫无根据。委员会强调，其计划仅在出现空缺职位时为移民提供岗位。

为近1,500名移民提供生活维持费的普通基金，目前每月需要近9万美元，由于缺乏足够的资金进行救济分配，该基金状况堪忧。

虽然有人指出，上海民众目前无力每月捐赠9万美元，但有人表示希望美国和英国的慈善组织在不久的将来能在此方面提供援助。

根据昨日在此间发布的一份知情报告，日本沿海货轮“三庄丸”号（s.s. Sansho）于昨晨从香港启航，预计将于明日下午抵达上海，载有约50名从欧洲船只转船至该殖民地的移民。

除这批人员外，预计另有约200名难民将于明日乘坐意大利劳埃德·特里埃斯蒂诺公司（Lloyd Triestino）的班轮“维多利亚”号（Victoria）抵达此处，该船将在上海及虹口码头停靠。

乘坐这艘意大利班轮抵沪的一批人中有一个有趣的情况，即同一批中有20人正前往大连。据悉，共有近300名移民已获得大连港口当局允许在此定居。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
JAN 1 2 1939
Further 2,000 Emigres
Coming To Far East By
Middle Of Next March

Small Numbers Allowed To Stay In Manila And
Singapore; Over 300 Proceeding To Dairen;
New Procedure Adopted Before Embarking

CONSULAR BODY WATCHING SITUATION;
SIR VICTOR SASSOON MAKES GRANT

At the present time reports indicate that a total of more than 2,000 emigres from Austria and Germany are coming out to the Far East before the middle of next March. This is in addition to the figure of 2,500 persons who have already arrived in this part of the world.

The majority of the future arrivals from Europe will, as in previous cases, make Shanghai their destination, although small numbers have managed to obtain official permission to settle in Singapore and Manila.

In addition to this a provisional arrangement is understood to have been made for about 300 emigres to be rehabilitated within the Port of Dairen.

The first of those to proceed to Dairen under this arrangement will be a group of about 20 emigres out of the total of 230 who are expected to arrive here on Sunday morning in the Lloyd Triestino's m.v. Victoria from Italy.

Vessels Chartered

Among shipping reports received in Shanghai yesterday, it was established that two vessels of the Hamburg-Amerika Linie, sailing from Hamburg, have been specially chartered to transport groups of refugees from Germany to Shanghai.

Of general significance, it was made known here yesterday that European refugees leaving Germany and Austria, will henceforward be required to remain at their port of embarkation for a minimum period of two weeks, in order to allow their names to be forwarded to the port authorities and shipping offices of the vessels they travel on to their destinations.

This procedure, it is firmly believed here, will give considerable aid to local relief bodies in their duties, as in previous cases only short notice was obtained of the number or professions of those expected to arrive.

Local Action

Meanwhile, although no official reply from the Consular Body to the Shanghai Municipal Council's letter of a fortnight ago in connection with the influx of European refugees has yet been received, it was reported that certain members of the Consular Body here have decided to take individual action, pending the return here of Commander L. Neyrone, Consul-General for Italy and Senior Consul in Shanghai, who is at present on holiday in Japan.

It may be pointed out, however, that the independent tasks of those members of the Consular Body now checking the refugee problem, will merely be in the nature of a preliminary study of the refugee situation prevailing in the Inter-national Settlement and French Concession, until the return here of the Senior Consul, when it is understood a thorough investigation will be made and a general consular discussion held on the matter.

In so far as passport regulations are concerned, these do not affect immigrants or visitors to Shanghai and, in this particular regard, the Municipal Council has already exercised what powers it can by notifying the Consular Body and Jewish organizations in Shanghai and abroad of the serious problem confronting this city, already burdened as it is with numerous Chinese refugees.

Sir Victor's Grant

The local committee aiding emigres from Europe received a special grant of money from Sir Victor, local utilities magnate, who is at the present time staying in London.

While the sum sent here by Sir Victor was not disclosed, it was revealed that it had come at a time when the committee's funds were running very low and therefore was particularly welcome toward the rehabilitation fund for German and Austrian Jewish emigres.

The rehabilitation fund, it may be recalled, was started recently by Sir Elly Kadoorie, K.B.E., Messrs. M. Speelman (Chairman), Ellis Hayim, E. Kelen (former Austrian Consul here), R. M. Joseph and K. M. Joseph, and aimed at financing refugees here in various businesses.

The rehabilitation fund is separate from the maintenance fund which now provides necessities for the emigres. A monthly total of $90,000, it was disclosed, was necessary to continue the latter-mentioned fund.

Regarding malignant rumours which persist here that local employers are dismissing members of their present staff to make place for emigres, this was strongly denied in a report by Mr. M. Speelman, head of the emigre committee, who explained that while quite a number of the emigres have already found employment, they merely filled vacancies and did not displace any other employees.

《上海泰晤士报》，
1939年1月12日

明年三月中旬前
另有2,000名移民
将来远东

获准留在马尼拉和新加坡的人数较少；
超过300人前往大连；登船前采用新程序

领事团关注局势；维克多·沙逊爵士提供拨款

目前的报告显示，在明年三月中旬之前，将有总计超过2,000名来自奥地利和德国的移民来到远东。这还不包括已经到达世界这一地区的2,500人。

与以往情况一样，未来从欧洲抵达的大多数人将以上海为目的地，尽管有少数人已设法获得官方许可在新加坡和马尼拉定居。

此外，据了解，已就约300名移民在大连港内进行安置作出了临时安排。

根据这一安排，首批前往大连的将是约20名移民，他们属于预计于周日上午乘坐意大利劳埃德·特里埃斯蒂诺公司的机动船“维多利亚”号（m.v. Victoria）抵达此处的230人总数中的一部分。

租用船只

根据昨日在上海收到的航运报告，证实汉堡-美洲航运公司（Hamburg-Amerika Linie）的两艘从汉堡启航的船只已被特别包租，用于将德国的难民群体运往上海。

具有普遍意义的是，昨日在此间获悉，离开德国和奥地利的欧洲难民今后将被要求在登船港口停留至少两周，以便将其姓名转发至目的地港口当局及其所乘船只的航运办事处。

此处坚信，这一程序将为本地救济机构的工作提供极大帮助，因为在以往的情况下，对于预期抵达人员的数量或职业往往只能得到很短时间的通知。

本地行动

与此同时，虽然尚未收到领事团对工部局两周前发出的关于欧洲难民涌入信函的正式回复，但有报道称，领事团的某些成员决定采取个人行动，以待意大利驻沪总领事兼上海首席领事 L. 内罗内指挥官（Commander L. Neyrone）返回此处，他目前正在日本度假。

不过需要指出的是，领事团中那些目前正在核查难民问题的成员所进行的独立工作，仅具有对国际租界和法租界 prevailing 难民局势进行初步研究的性质，直到首席领事返回此处。据了解，届时将对这一问题进行彻底调查，并举行全面的领事讨论。

就护照规定而言，这些规定并不影响进入上海的移民或访客，在这一特定方面，工部局已经行使了其所能行使的权力，通知了上海及海外的领事团和犹太组织本市面临的严重问题，因为本市已经负担了大量中国难民。

维克多爵士的拨款

援助欧洲移民的本地委员会收到了本地公用事业巨头维克多爵士的一笔特别拨款，他目前正旅居伦敦。

虽然维克多爵士汇至此处的金额未予披露，但据透露，这笔款项是在委员会资金非常紧张时到来的，因此对于德国和奥地利犹太移民的安置基金来说尤为受欢迎。

回想一下，安置基金最近由埃利·嘉道理爵士（K.B.E.）、M. 斯皮尔曼先生（主席）、埃利斯·哈伊姆、E. 凯伦（前奥地利驻沪领事）、R. M. 约瑟夫和 K. M. 约瑟夫发起，旨在为难民在此从事各类商业活动提供资金。

安置基金与现在为移民提供必需品的生活维持基金是分开的。据披露，维持后者每月总共需要9万美元。

关于此处持续存在的恶性谣言，称本地雇主正在解雇现有员工以为移民腾出位置，移民委员会负责人 M. 斯皮尔曼先生在一份报告中强烈否认了这一点，他解释说，虽然相当数量的移民已经找到工作，但他们只是填补了空缺职位，并没有取代任何其他员工。

MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. E. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D.
Date

SHANGHAI TIMES.

JAN 10 1939

S.M.C. LETTER STILL
BEING DEBATED

Question Of Limiting
Number Of European
Jewish Refugees

No official answer from the Consular Body to the Shanghai Municipal Council's letter of a fortnight ago in connection with the influx of European Jewish refugees has yet been received, "The Shanghai Times" learnt on good authority yesterday. A reply is expected in the near future.

The Council, while only too willing to do what it can in the matter, has felt its duty to notify both the Consular body and Jewish organizations both in Shanghai and abroad of the problems that might arise with the arrival of an unlimited number of refugees. The International Settlement and French Concession are already overcrowded with Chinese refugees, it is pointed out.

Whether any concrete suggestions have been made by the Council in the matter could not be ascertained yesterday. As Shanghai is not a "country" nor its people "a nation," the S.M.C. in itself has practically no powers to prevent the influx of a huge crowd of people from abroad.

That is a matter which is in the hands of the Consulates representing the countries whose ships are bringing refugees here. The Consular Body is, as far as can be determined, the sole body which can adequately and properly deal with the matter.
pages.zh:
市政警察
东南区登记处
编号 S. B. D.
日期

《上海泰晤士报》，
1939年1月10日

工部局信函
仍在讨论中

限制欧洲犹太
难民人数的问题

《上海泰晤士报》昨日从可靠渠道获悉，领事团尚未对工部局两周前发出的关于欧洲犹太难民涌入的信函作出正式答复。预计不久将会有回复。

工部局虽然非常愿意在此事上尽其所能，但认为有责任通知上海及海外的领事团和犹太组织，无限数量的难民抵达可能引发的问题。有人指出，国际租界和法租界已经挤满了中国难民。

昨日无法查明工部局是否在此事上提出了任何具体建议。由于上海不是一个“国家”，其人民也不是一个“民族”，工部局本身实际上没有权力阻止大量人群从国外涌入。

这是一个掌握在代表那些用船只将难民运至此处的国家的领事馆手中的问题。据目前所能确定的，领事团是唯一能够充分且妥善解决此事的机构。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES,

JAN 8 1939

How Jewish Refugees In
Shanghai Are Being Fed,
Housed And Looked After

'Co-ordinated Activities Of Three Bodies, With
Long-Term Problems And Desirabilities Being
Kept In Sight; Dangers Fully Recognized

LOCAL JEWISH COMMUNITY HAS RISEN
MAGNIFICENTLY TO OCCASION

Special to "The Shanghai Sunday Times"

During the past few months 1500 Jewish refugees have arrived in Shanghai, and all have been taken care of. They have been housed, fed, and provided with pocket-money; there are doctors and dentists to see to their health, and teachers to teach them English. The local Jewish community has risen magnificently to the occasion.

The work is in the hands of three bodies. The Committee for the Assistance of Jewish Refugees in Shanghai, presided over by Mr. M. Speelman, is a co-ordinating committee and handles most of the finance, while most of the actual work of relief is done either by the Relief Society for German Austrian Jews or by the International Committee for Granting Relief to European Refugees. The former body, already five years old, under the very efficient and able direction of Dr. Kurt Marx, deals only with Jews, interpreting the word Jew in as wide a sense as possible, namely any person who irrespective of religion can claim a Jewish father. The second body deals with any refugee from European dictatorships.

The first of these two latter bodies is the one that is doing by far the greater proportion of the present relief work. Strictly speaking its work begins in Europe, for it is in almost daily communication with relief bodies there, but for practical purposes it is at Singapore that the refugee first comes into contact with it. A Singapore society, acting on advice from here, meets all ships carrying refugees and distributes leaflets giving instructions and forms on which necessary details are to be filled in, at the same time cabling Shanghai the approximate number of those en route to this port. At the next stopping place, usually Manila, the forms are collected and definite statistics cabled to Dr. Marx, who then arranges for three commissioners to meet the incoming boat, one to see to bachelors, one to childless married couples, and one to married couples with children, arrangements having already been made for the accommodation and feeding of the newcomers.

Problem Of Housing

At the moment two methods are being resorted to for coping with the situation. Some of the newcomers are being housed in individual quarters, either in private houses or rooms in private houses, which are rented by the Society for this purpose. They are, in addition, allowed a certain amount of money with which to feed themselves, This method, however, is exceedingly costly, and the Society prefers the system of mass quarters and mass catering, such as in operation in Embankment Building at the moment. Here several hundred refugees are established, in barracks as it were, and go to the Chinese Y.M.C.A., in Szechuen Road, for

《上海泰晤士报》，

1939年1月8日

上海的犹太难民如何获得
食物、住所及照料

“三个机构协调行动，同时兼顾
长期问题与需求；充分认识到潜在危险

本地犹太社区出色地应对了这一局面

专供《上海星期日泰晤士报》

在过去几个月里，有1500名犹太难民抵达上海，所有人都得到了照料。他们获得了住所、食物和零用钱；有医生和牙医负责他们的健康，还有教师教他们英语。本地犹太社区出色地应对了这一局面。

这项工作由三个机构负责。由M. Speelman先生主持的“上海援助犹太难民委员会”是一个协调委员会，负责大部分财务工作，而大部分实际的救济工作则由“德奥犹太难民救济协会”或“欧洲难民国际救济委员会”承担。前一个机构已有五年历史，在Kurt Marx博士非常高效和能干的领导下，仅服务于犹太人，其对“犹太人”一词的解释尽可能宽泛，即无论宗教信仰如何，只要其父亲是犹太人即可。后一个机构则服务于来自欧洲独裁政权的任何难民。

在这两个后述机构中，第一个承担了目前绝大部分的救济工作。严格来说，其工作始于欧洲，因为它与那里的救济机构几乎每天都有联系，但就实际而言，难民首先在新加坡与其接触。新加坡的一个社团根据这里的建议，迎接所有载有难民的船只，分发包含指示和需填写必要细节表格的传单，同时电告上海预计抵达本港的人数。在下一个停靠点（通常是马尼拉），表格被收集起来，并将确切的统计数据电告Marx博士，随后他安排三名专员去迎接 incoming 船只，一人负责单身汉，一人负责无子女的已婚夫妇，一人负责有子女的已婚夫妇，此时为新来者的住宿和饮食所做的安排已经就绪。

住房问题

目前正采取两种方法来应对这一局面。部分新来者被安置在单独的住处，要么是私人住宅，要么是由协会为此目的租用的私人住宅中的房间。此外，他们还获准拥有一定数量的资金用于自行解决饮食。然而，这种方法成本极高，协会更倾向于采用集体住宿和集体供餐的制度，正如目前在堤岸大厦（Embankment Building）实施的那样。这里有数百名难民定居，宛如住在兵营里，并前往四川路的中华基督教青年会就餐，尽管协会希望最终建立自己的供餐系统。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
JAN 8 1939

their meals, though eventually the
Society hopes to establish its own
catering system. This method is
obviously much more economical,
and, in view of the months of ex-
penditure ahead—expenditure that
will increase as the numbers of re-
fugees now en route arrive here—
one that would have to be adopted,
even if the Society did not, as in
fact it does, prefer to give relief as
much in kind as possible, and to
distribute the minimum of actual
cash.

The refugees include in their
numbers persons of all ranks in life.
of all trades, professions and
occupations, but the great majority
come from the middle class, and are
people who have never travelled
and never expected to travel. They
are essentially parochially minded,
to whom everything is new and
strange, who feel completely lost
amid their new surroundings. Such
people are bound to make mistakes.
The vast majority, however, have
come with the determination to
make the best of things and speedily
learn to accommodate themselves.
The great drawback is the language
difficulty; few speak English, and
one of the first things to be done,
once they have settled in, is to put
them in the way of learning that
essential language. This has been
seen to by the Shanghai Jewish
Youths Association, which is
organizing and financing training
in English for all newcomers.

Employment Office

An Employment Office is a very
important part of the Society's
organization. Careful statistics are
being compiled of the qualifications
and capabilities of all immigrants.
and contact has been established
with all the big commercial centres
in the Far East. So far however,
few of the newcomers have been
placed in employment. The mis-
sionary societies have found use for
a few doctors, and a few have been
set up in business, but, at the out-
side, barely 100 have been placed
up till now.

In this matter of finding employ-
ment the Society's officials are fully
alive to the necessity of hastening
slowly. Only where it is assured
that a definite opening exists will it
advance capital to enable businesses
to be opened, nor does it seek to
find work for its charges by offer-
ing cheap labour. They are fully
alive to the danger of depressing
wages and the standard of living.
They recognize, in fact, that they
have a double responsibility, one to
the refugees and one to Shanghai.
That Shanghai is in no state to
absorb these newcomers at the pre-
sent time they know, and when
their advice is asked it is always
against coming here. They under-
stand and sympathize with the at-
titude of the Shanghai Municipal
Council in seeking to restrict the
number of immigrants. On the
other hand once people decide to
come here and are on their way
they do their very best for them,
and in doing their best for the re-
fugee they are also doing their best
for Shanghai. Without the work
being done by these Relief Societies
we should be faced with a problem
of foreign destitution which would
be disastrous in its repercussions on
the whole foreign community.

Hope For Future

It is the view of the Societies'
officials that, with the cessation of
hostilities, a place should be found
ultimately for the newcomers in
Shanghai's economy, or rather in
the economy of the Far East, Shang-
hai being, it is hoped, merely a tem-
porary resting place for many.
Meanwhile, in providing for the care
of the newcomers and in taking the
long view that their assimilation
into the local labour market is not
to be rushed and must only take
place as circumstances permit, the
local Jewish community is helping
not only its own people but also the
whole of foreign Shanghai, and in
their work deserve Foreign Shang-
hai's wholehearted assistance and
support.

1939年1月8日

显然，这种方法要经济得多，鉴于未来数月将有支出——随着目前正在途中的难民人数抵达这里，支出将会增加——即使协会不像事实上那样偏好尽可能以实物形式提供救济并分发最少的现金，也不得不采用这种方法。

难民中包括各行各业、各种职业的人，但绝大多数来自中产阶级，他们是那些从未旅行过也从未想过要旅行的人。他们本质上具有狭隘的地方观念，周围的一切对他们来说都是新奇和陌生的，他们在新的环境中感到完全迷失。这样的人难免会犯错误。然而，绝大多数人怀着尽力适应现状的决心而来，并迅速学会适应自己。最大的障碍是语言困难；很少有人会说英语，一旦他们安顿下来，首要任务之一就是让他们有机会学习这门必不可少的语言。此事已由上海犹太青年协会负责，该协会正在为所有新来者组织和资助英语培训。

就业办公室

就业办公室是该协会组织中非常重要的一部分。正在仔细编制所有移民的资格和能力统计数据，并与远东所有大型商业中心建立了联系。然而，到目前为止，只有少数新来者找到了工作。传教士团体聘用了几位医生，还有几个人开始了自己的生意，但充其量，到目前为止安置就业的人数 barely 100人。

在寻找就业方面，协会官员充分意识到必须谨慎行事、循序渐进。只有在确定存在明确机会的情况下，它才会预付资本以开办企业，也不会通过提供廉价劳动力来为其受助者寻找工作。他们充分意识到压低工资和生活水平的危险。事实上，他们认识到自己负有双重责任，一是对难民，二是对上海。他们知道上海目前无力吸收这些新来者，当有人征求他们的建议时，他们总是劝阻人们不要来这里。他们理解并同情上海公共租界工部局试图限制移民数量的态度。另一方面，一旦人们决定来这里并在途中，他们会尽全力帮助他们，而在为难民尽力的同时，他们也是在为上海尽力。如果没有这些救济协会所做的工作，我们将面临外国贫民的问题，这将对整个外侨社区产生灾难性的反响。

对未来的希望

协会官员认为，随着敌对行动的停止，最终应在上海的经济中，或者更确切地说，在远东的经济中，为新来者找到一席之地，希望上海仅仅是许多人的临时歇脚处。与此同时，在照顾新来者并采取长远观点，即他们融入当地劳动力市场不应操之过急，只能视情况而定方面，本地犹太社区不仅在帮助其同胞，也在帮助整个外侨上海，在他们的工作中值得外侨上海全心全意的协助和支持。

CONFIDENTIAL
DRAWER

SHANGHAI TIMES,
DEC 3 1 1938

Huge Camp
For Jewish
Immigrants

Building To Take Care
Of 2,000 Is Planned
In Hongkew Area

CONSULAR BODY TOLD
OF SITUATION

Refugees Already Have
German Newspaper
In Shanghai

The Committee for the As-
sistance of European Jewish
Refugees in Shanghai and its
allied associations here are
making arrangements for the
accommodation of more than
1,500 immigrants in a centraliz-
ed camp in the Hongkew area,
it was learnt here yesterday.
This camp will be on the
premises of the school at 138
Ward Road, which has been
loaned by the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council.

This move is being made princi-
pally as an economy measure as
it will be far cheaper to house
and provide food for the refugees,
if they are brought together in one
place. At the present time most of
the refugees are provided for in
boarding houses in the Hongkew
area, the majority of these being
operated by Russians.

It will take about one month to
put the Ward Road school into shape
and certain alterations will be made
in order to provide the best possible
accommodation under the circum-
stances. Some of the members of
the committees in charge feel that
as many as 2,000 refugees could be
taken care of in the school, but for
the time being it is hardly likely
that the number will exceed 1,500.

Final arrangements were being
made yesterday for the reception of
about 330 more refugees due to
arrive here this morning on board
the s.s. Conte Rosso and s.s. Pots-
dam. The former vessel is
bringing 270 refugees and the latter
is understood to have about 60 on
board.

Newspaper Established

The situation with regard to the
future is still extremely doubtful and
the members of the various com-
mittees working on the problem are
still at a loss to know how many
more refugees will arrive in Shang-
hai during the next few weeks.

It is apparent that those refugees
who have been in Shanghai for some
time are becoming a little more set-
tled and many are already beginning
to familiarize themselves with the
city. One interesting announcement
made here yesterday was to the
effect that a newspaper to serve the
refugees has already been establish-
ed in Shanghai. This is, of course,
published in the German language
and is the newest addition to Shang-
hai's large group of international
publications.

Only a very few of the refugees
speak English and this language
difficulty is naturally a great dis-
advantage to them in finding employ-
ment and otherwise establishing
themselves here. Immediately after
their arrival many of the refugees
were very reluctant to stray far from
the camps or boarding houses where
they were living, but now they are
frequently seen on the streets and
sometimes in the shops and banks.
A few are said to have small sums
of money to assist them over the
first difficult period which they must
undergo in Shanghai.

Considering the size of the prob-
lem and the suddenness with which
it came to a head a few weeks ago,
the committees in charge has per-
formed remarkable work in taking
care of so many immigrants. Mr.
M. Speelman, who is in full charge
of the financing side of the work, has
devoted a very great deal of his
time to the problem and has never
been too busy to assist others who
are working upon it.

Others who have been closely con-
nected with the work include Messrs.
D. E. J. Abraham, Mr. Ellis Hayim
and Mr. J. Holtzer. The allied
committees taking care of the re-
fugees are made up of "The Com-
mittee for the Assistance of European
Jewish Refugees in Shanghai," the
"Hilfsfond fuer Deutsche Juden" and
"The International Committee for
Granting Relief to European Refu-
gees."

As was stated in an article in "The
Shanghai Times" last week, the
Shanghai Municipal Council has
taken the Jewish refugees problem
under consideration and, in fairness
to the organizations granting relief
and residents in Shanghai in general,
believes there should be a limit set
on the number of immigrants arriv-
ing here. It was learnt here yester-
day that a letter to this effect has
been sent to the various members
of the Consular Body and that
action will be taken in the matter
in the near future.

档案柜

《上海泰晤士报》，
1938年12月31日

大型犹太
移民营地

计划在虹口地区
建造可容纳2,000人的设施

领事团获悉
相关情况

难民已在
上海拥有德文报纸

据昨日获悉，上海援助欧洲犹太难民委员会及其在沪的相关协会正在安排将1500多名移民安置在虹口地区的一个集中营地中。该营地将设在华德路138号的学校校舍内，该校舍由上海公共租界工部局出借。

此举主要是出于节约措施的考虑，因为如果将难民集中在一处，为他们提供住房和食物的费用将便宜得多。目前，大多数难民由虹口地区的寄宿公寓提供食宿，其中大多数由俄国人经营。

将华德路学校整理妥当大约需要一个月时间，并将进行某些改造，以便在这种情况下提供尽可能好的住宿条件。负责委员会的一些成员认为，该校舍最多可容纳2000名难民，但目前人数不太可能超过1500人。

昨天正在做最后安排，以接待预计今天上午乘坐“罗索伯爵号”（s.s. Conte Rosso）和“波茨坦号”（s.s. Potsdam）轮船抵达的约330名难民。前者载有270名难民，据悉后者船上约有60名。

创办报纸

未来的局势仍然极其不明朗，处理此问题的各委员会成员仍不知晓未来几周内会有多少难民抵达上海。

显然，那些已在上海停留一段时间的难民正变得稍微安定一些，许多人已开始熟悉这座城市。昨天在此发布的一个有趣公告称，一份服务于难民的报纸已在上海创办。当然，这份报纸以德文出版，是上海众多国际出版物中的最新成员。

只有极少数难民会说英语，这种语言困难自然使他们在寻找工作和在此立足方面处于极大劣势。抵达后不久，许多难民非常不愿意远离他们居住的营地或寄宿公寓，但现在经常可以在街上看到他们，有时甚至在商店和银行里也能看到。据说有少数人手头有少量资金，以帮助他们在上海必须经历的初期困难阶段。

考虑到问题的规模以及几周前问题突然爆发的突然性，负责委员会在照顾如此多移民方面完成了卓越的工作。全面负责该项工作财务方面的M. Speelman先生投入了大量时间处理这一问题，并且从不因忙碌而拒绝协助其他从事此项工作的人。

其他与此工作密切相关的人士包括D. E. J. Abraham先生、Ellis Hayim先生和J. Holtzer先生。照顾难民的联合委员会由“上海援助欧洲犹太难民委员会”、“德国犹太人援助基金”（Hilfsfond fuer Deutsche Juden）和“欧洲难民国际救济委员会”组成。

正如上周《上海泰晤士报》的一篇文章所述，上海公共租界工部局已考虑犹太难民问题，并且出于对提供救济的组织以及上海一般居民的公平考虑，认为应对抵达这里的移民数量设定限制。昨日获悉，一封以此为目的的信函已发送给领事团的各位成员，近期将就此事项采取行动。
