00827
SHANGHAI TIMES,
DEC 24 1938
Limitation Of European
Jewish Refugees May Be
Instituted By Council
Willingness To Assist Immigrants Should Be
Combined With Due Regard To Welfare Of
People Already Residing In Shanghai
CITY CAN ONLY ABSORB VERY LIMITED
NUMBER OF REFUGEES AT PRESENT
Special to "The Shanghai Times"
It was learnt here yesterday that the Shanghai Municipal
Council may have to take steps to limit the arrival of European
Jewish immigrants in this port in order to keep the situation
from getting out of control. "The Shanghai Times" ascertained
on good authority that informal discussions regarding the
matter have been carried out among the various Council
members.
The Council is only too willing to do what it can to assist
the refugees who have already arrived in Shanghai and is
desirous of assuming its share of the responsibility, it is stated.
Emphasis is laid on the fact that the local Jewish community
in Shanghai is doing its best to assist the refugees and that it
has already shown itself exceedingly generous in this respect.
It is pointed out, on the other
hand, that the assistance which the
local Jewish community can render
is limited at best. In addition, the
various international charitable
organizations in Shanghai have been
so pressed for funds since the out-
break of the Sino-Japanese hostili-
ties that it is unlikely that they will
be able to extend their fields of
endeavour in the near future.
Economic Absorption
A representative of "The Shanghai
Times" was further informed yester-
day, through the most reliable
sources, that the members of the
Shanghai Municipal Council feel
that this city is one of the last in the
world which should be expected to
assume a large share of the burden
of the present European emigration
problem.
The recent hostilities have badly
affected the powers of economic
absorption of Shanghai and it is in-
conceivable that several thousand
foreign immigrants could be provid-
ed with employment within the
predictable future. Taking this
factor into consideration, the
Council feels that many immigrants
must by necessity remain unemploy-
ed or else, perhaps, usurp the posi-
tions held by others working
in Shanghai.
These considerations and various
other aspects of the question have
led the Council to take cognizance
of what steps lie within its power
to limit the arrival of more refugees.
Attention is called to the fact that
the International Settlement has a
right to protect itself, although for
the time being any measures which
might be applied must be the sub-
ject of the most careful study.
Consular Body Approached
In view of the pressing nature of
the problem, the Shanghai Municipal
Council yesterday requested the
members of the Consular Body to
give it due consideration. The haste
in which this emergency has come
to a head has made it impossible to
carry out full consultations with the
authorities of the French Conces-
sion, but as the French Consul-
General is a member of the Consular
Body he will automatically be
familiarized with the situation
through that organ.
One thing which makes things
unduly perplexing is the fact that
at the present time it is impossible
to ascertain how many more re-
fugees are actually on their way to
Shanghai. It will also be remem-
bered that the earlier influx of re-
fugees was minor in nature and did
not give rise to anything approach-
ing an emergency. During the past
week, however, over 500 European
Jewish refugees arrived in Shanghai
and 200 more are expected in the
latter part of next week. This will
bring the total number of refugees
in Shanghai to over 1,200, and
charitable organizations estimate
that at least 90 per cent. of these
people must be maintained on relief.

00827
《上海泰晤士报》，
1938年12月24日
工部局或将对欧洲
犹太难民实施限制
援助移民的意愿应与适当顾及
已居住在上海居民的福祉相结合
目前本市仅能接纳极少量难民
《上海泰晤士报》专讯
据本报昨日获悉，为防止局势失控，上海公共租界工部局可能不得不采取措施，限制欧洲犹太移民抵达本港。《上海泰晤士报》从可靠渠道得知，工部局各位董事之间已就此事项进行了非正式讨论。
据悉，工部局非常愿意尽其所能援助已抵达上海的难民，并渴望承担其应尽的那份责任。报道强调，上海本地犹太社区正竭尽全力援助难民，且在此方面已表现出极大的慷慨。另一方面也指出，本地犹太社区所能提供的援助终究是有限的。此外，自中日敌对行动爆发以来，上海各国际慈善组织的资金一直十分紧张，因此在不久的将来，它们不太可能扩大其救助范围。
经济吸纳能力
《上海泰晤士报》代表昨日还通过最可靠的渠道获悉，上海公共租界工部局董事们认为，在当今世界，本市是最不应被期望承担当前欧洲移民问题大部分负担的城市之一。
近期的敌对行动严重影响了上海的经济吸纳能力，在可预见的未来，要为数千名外国移民提供就业机会是不可想象的。考虑到这一因素，工部局认为，许多移民必然处于失业状态，否则可能会抢占其他在上海工作人士的职位。
出于这些考量以及该问题的其他各个方面，工部局已注意到在其权力范围内采取何种步骤以限制更多难民的抵达。提请注意的是，国际租界有权保护自身，尽管目前任何可能实施的措施都必须经过最仔细的研究。
接洽领事团
鉴于问题的紧迫性，上海公共租界工部局昨日请求领事团成员对此给予适当考虑。由于这一紧急情况来得突然，致使无法与法租界当局进行充分磋商，但鉴于法国总领事是领事团成员，他将通过该机构自动了解相关情况。
使事情变得过分复杂的一个事实是，目前无法确定究竟还有多少难民正在前往上海的途中。还应记得，早期的难民涌入规模较小，并未引发任何接近紧急状态的情况。然而，在过去的一周内，超过500名欧洲犹太难民抵达上海，预计下周后半周还将有200人抵达。这将使在上海的难民总数超过1,200人，据慈善组织估计，这些人中至少有90%必须依靠救济维持生活。

SHANGHAI TIMES,
DEC 24 1938
Jewish
Relief
Scheme
Committees Organized
With Finance Group
Centralized
An announcement was made here
yesterday of the new system of
organization which has been created
in Shanghai to handle the problem
presented by the arrival of a large
number of Jewish European re-
fugees. The three committees which
have been put in charge are known
as "The Committee for the Assist-
ance of European Jewish Refugees
in Shanghai," the "Hilfsfond fuer
Duetsche Juden" and "The Inter-
national Committee for Granting
Relief to European Refugees."
In view of the magnitude of the
problem confronting these organiza-
tions, it has been decided to
nominate a special Public Relations
Committee which will handle all
problems connected with the re-
fugees. This committee is compos-
ed of Mr. M. Speelman, (Chairman),
Mr. D. E. J. Abraham, Mr. Ellis
Hayim, and Mr. J. Holzer.
All matters relating to the housing,
catering and caring for the refugees
will continue to be handled by two
offices, one under the direction of
Mr. Paul Kessler and the other under
the direction of Dr. Kurt Marx.
These gentlemen will also be in
charge of the distribution of funds
to the refugees.
Mr. Speelman is taking full
charge of the financial side of the
question such as the collection of
funds, and monthly subscribers as
well as intending contributors are
requested to send their cheques or
donations direct to him at No. 7
Avenue Edward VII.

《上海泰晤士报》，
1938年12月24日
犹太
救济
计划
委员会成立
财务工作集中管理
昨日在此宣布了一项新的组织架构，旨在处理大量欧洲犹太难民抵达上海所带来的问题。负责此项工作的三个委员会分别为“上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会”（The Committee for the Assistance of European Jewish Refugees in Shanghai）、“德国犹太人援助基金”（Hilfsfond fuer Duetsche Juden）以及“欧洲难民国际救济委员会”（The International Committee for Granting Relief to European Refugees）。
鉴于这些组织所面临问题的规模之大，已决定提名一个专门的公共关系委员会，负责处理与难民有关的所有问题。该委员会由M. Speelman先生（主席）、D. E. J. Abraham先生、Ellis Hayim先生和J. Holzer先生组成。
所有涉及难民住房、膳食供应及照料的事务，将继续由两个办事处处理，一个由Paul Kessler先生负责，另一个由Kurt Marx博士负责。这两位先生还将负责向难民分发资金。
Speelman先生全面负责该问题的财务方面，如资金筹集等，月度认捐者及意向捐赠者请将支票或捐款直接寄至爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）7号给他。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
DEC 21 1938
Extremely Serious View
Being Taken Of Jewish
Refugee Situation Here
Members Of Committee Worked Night And Day To
Find Accommodation For Latest Arrivals But
More Are Expected Here Late Next Week
FEEDING OF CAMP INMATES DESTINED
TO INVOLVE BIG MONTHLY OUTLAY
Special to "The Shanghai Times"
Leading foreign relief workers interviewed here yesterday
by "The Shanghai Times" indicated that a very real emergency
has been created by the arrival of hundreds of European
immigrants. It is believed that unless outside assistance is
forthcoming in the very near future the matter may get beyond
the control of local organizations dealing with the situation.
This question has already been given due consideration by
the International Red Cross, and during the last few days
members of the Committee for the Assistance of European
Jewish Refugees in Shanghai have been working day and night.
It was only at the last minute yesterday that accommodation
was found for the 560 immigrants arriving on the Conte
Biancamano in the afternoon.
A thorough investigation had been
made of all available housing in
Hongkew and this resulted in the
locating of enough houses to take
care of only about 150 of the new
arrivals. Consequently an appeal
was made to certain property owners
on the south side of Soochow Creek
and space enough to take care of
a very large number of people was
made available on the ground floor
of the Embankment Building.
If the matter of housing consti-
tutes a very serious aspect of the
problem, the question of feeding the
refugees is expected to become a
far more difficult thing to solve.
One member of the relief committee,
who is in close touch with this,
stated yesterday that if the number
of destitute refugees here grows as
rapidly as in the past it may cost
as much as $100,000 a month to feed
them.
Council Lends Building
At first thought this might appear
to be a very high figure, but it is
based on an estimated expenditure
of $20 per head a month. The crea-
tion of special soup kitchens to
provide at least one hot meal a day
at the lowest possible cost is fore-
shadowed, and, in addition, it may
be necessary to set up matshed
camps in which to house and feed
the refugees during the summer
months.
One encouraging note in connec-
tion with the latter is an expression
of willingness to help on the part
of the Shanghai Municipal Council
yesterday afternoon. In a special
announcement the Council stated
that a building at 138 Ward Road,
leased as a primary school, had been
placed at the disposal of the com-
mittee. It was understood that this
building would accommodate about
350 foreign refugees.
The need for an almost unlimited
amount of housing is evidenced by
the fact that 260 more refugees are
expected on board the Conte Rosso,
which is due to arrive in Shanghai
on December 31. There are also
reports to the effect that large num-
bers of refugees are coming on
German boats during the early part
of the year, but at the present time,
no figures have been available in
this connection.
Refugees From Manchuria
Additional information has reach-
ed Shanghai from Manchuria, where
it is believed that large numbers of
refugees are making their way to
the Far East, via Siberia. If these
people are unable to find employ-
ment in such places as Harbin, Muk-
den and Dairen it is more than
likely that they will proceed to
Shanghai, as has been the case in
the past with so many White Rus-
sian emigres.
In any event it is expected that
there will be in the neighbourhood
of 1,200 Jewish immigrants in
Shanghai by January 1, and, taking
current statistics as a fair indica-
tion, about 95 per cent. of these
people will be wholly destitute.
The question is often raised as
to why these people are being sent
to Shanghai when of all cities in
the world it is perhaps least cap-
able of coping with the additional
burden which their care will in-
volve. Those who are familiar with
the situation state that the influx
is by no means due to any belief
on the part of the refugees that
Shanghai is a place where they can
come and find the means whereby
to begin life anew.
Actually the reason for their com-
ing to Shanghai lies in the fact

《上海泰晤士报》，
1938年12月21日
对本埠犹太难民
局势持极其严肃态度
委员会成员日夜工作为最新抵达者
寻找住所，但预计下周后期将有更多人抵沪
收容营囚徒的伙食费
预计将带来巨大的月度开支
《上海泰晤士报》专讯
《上海泰晤士报》昨日在此采访的主要外籍救济工作人员表示，数百名欧洲移民的抵达造成了真正的紧急状况。人们认为，除非在不久的将来获得外部援助，否则此事可能会超出处理此局势的本地组织的控制能力。
这一问题已引起红十字国际委员会的适当重视，而在过去几天里，“上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会”的成员们日夜工作。直到昨天最后一刻，才为下午乘坐“比安卡马诺伯爵号”（Conte Biancamano）抵达的560名移民找到了住所。
有关部门对虹口所有可用住房进行了彻底调查，结果只找到足以安置约150名新来者的房屋。因此，向苏州河南岸的某些业主发出呼吁，并在堤岸大厦（Embankment Building）的一楼腾出了足以安置大量人员的空间。
如果住房问题构成了该问题非常严峻的一面，那么难民的吃饭问题预计将成为一个更难解决的难题。一位与此事密切相关的救济委员会成员昨日表示，如果此地赤贫困民的数量像过去那样迅速增长，供养他们的费用每月可能高达10万美元。
工部局出借楼宇
乍看之下，这似乎是一个很高的数字，但这是基于每人每月20美元的估算支出。预计将设立专门的施粥处，以尽可能低的成本每天至少提供一顿热餐；此外，在夏季月份，可能还有必要搭建棚屋营地，以便安置和供养难民。
关于后者，有一个令人鼓舞的消息，即上海公共租界工部局昨日下午表达了愿意提供帮助的意愿。工部局在一项特别公告中表示，位于华德路138号、原租赁作为小学使用的一栋建筑，已交由该委员会支配。据悉，该建筑可容纳约350名外籍难民。
对几乎无限量的住房需求，由以下事实可见一斑：预计另有260名难民将乘坐“罗索伯爵号”（Conte Rosso）抵达，该船定于12月31日抵沪。另有报告称，年初将有大量难民乘坐德国船只前来，但目前尚无相关具体数字。
来自满洲的难民
上海收到了来自满洲的补充信息，据信有大量难民正经由西伯利亚前往远东。如果这些人无法在哈尔滨、奉天和大连等地找到工作，他们极有可能像过去许多白俄流亡者那样，转而前往上海。
无论如何，预计到1月1日，上海将有约1,200名犹太移民，以目前的统计数据作为合理指标，这些人中约95%将完全陷入赤贫。
人们经常提出这样一个问题：为什么这些人要被送往上海？毕竟在世界所有城市中，上海或许最无力应对照顾他们所涉及的额外负担。熟悉情况的人士指出，难民的涌入绝非因为难民相信上海是一个他们可以前来并找到重新开始生活手段的地方。
实际上，他们来到上海的原因在于

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
DEC 21 1938

that no other city in the world is open to them as this is the only port where they can land without a visa. As is generally known, the shipping companies are unable to take passengers unless they are sure that they may be landed at some definite port. Since the outbreak of the hostilities the landing restrictions in Shanghai have become very lax and for this reason this port has become the focal point in the Jewish exodus from Europe.
International Red Cross
At the present moment it is quite impossible to look too far into the future, but one relief expert interviewed here yesterday expressed the opinion that under the very best of circumstances Shanghai would never be able to absorb several thousand Jewish emigrants and provide the means whereby they could become self-supporting.
This raises the question as to whether or not the majority of the refugees who have arrived here in months gone by can be sent on to more auspicious localities eventually. Various places for settlement, including the Virgin Islands and Madagascar have been suggested, and it is hoped that international organizations working on the problem will give the situation at Shanghai their fullest consideration.
The International Red Cross here has been approached by the American Advisory Committee on Civil-
ian Relief and asked to bring the matter to the attention of officials of the organization in the United States. As a result of this request a report has been prepared and handed to the United States Consulate-General to be forwarded to the United States.
According to information obtained here yesterday, consideration is being taken of the fact that the Red Cross in America has a number of Jewish supporters who would probably like to see some assistance given to the refugees in Shanghai. In the meantime, the International Red Cross at Shanghai is giving whatever assistance it can to the Jewish relief committees here, although most of its funds have of course been earmarked for Chinese relief. One way in which the International Red Cross has been able to help out was through the sending a number of refugee doctors to the interior to carry on relief work.
In the meantime most of the emergency relief funds are coming from the various Jewish communities in Shanghai and from contributions made by the general public. The Committee for the Assistance of European Jewish Refugees in Shanghai is anxious to have any sort of aid it can get and welcomes the contribution of beds, clothing, bedding, furniture and other household goods from local residents.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，
1938年12月21日

世界上没有其他城市像上海这样向他们开放，因为这里是唯一无需签证即可登陆的港口。众所周知，除非航运公司确信乘客可以在某个确定的港口登陆，否则无法承运乘客。自敌对行动爆发以来，上海的登陆限制变得非常宽松，因此本港已成为犹太人从欧洲出逃的焦点。
红十字国际委员会
目前很难对未来做太长远的展望，但昨日在此接受采访的一位救济专家表示，即使在最好的情况下，上海也永远无法吸纳数千名犹太移民并提供使他们能够自食其力的手段。
这就提出了一个问题：过去几个月抵达此地的绝大多数难民，最终是否能被送往更有利的地区。有人建议了包括维尔京群岛和马达加斯加在内的多个定居地点，希望从事此问题工作的国际组织能充分考虑上海的局势。
驻沪美国平民救济咨询委员会已接洽此地的红十字国际委员会，并请其将此事项提请注意该组织在美国的官员。应此请求，一份报告已 prepared 并递交给美国总领事馆，以便转送美国。
根据昨日在此获得的信息，各方正在考虑这样一个事实：美国的红十字会拥有一些犹太支持者，他们可能希望看到对上海的难民提供某种援助。与此同时，上海的红十字国际委员会正在尽其所能援助此地的犹太救济委员会，尽管其大部分资金当然已指定用于中国救济事业。红十字国际委员会能够提供帮助的一种方式，是派遣多名难民医生前往内地开展救济工作。
与此同时，大部分紧急救济资金来自上海各地的犹太社区以及公众的捐款。“上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会”渴望获得任何形式的援助，并欢迎当地居民捐赠床铺、衣物、寝具、家具及其他家居用品。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
DEC 21 1938

500 Jewish
Refugees
Land Here

Accommodation Prepared
For Groups Taken In
Trucks From Jetty

Over 500 Jewish refugees from Germany and Austria, few of them speaking English and a large proportion of them women and children, arrived here yesterday afternoon aboard the Lloyd Triestino liner Conte Biancamano, as an advance guard of about 3,000 or 4,000 more European immigrants, who are expected here shortly.

Members of the Committee for the Assistance of European Jewish Refugees in Shanghai, as well as numerous European Jews, who had arrived in Shanghai during the last few months, gathered at the Shanghai and Hongkew Wharf to meet the new arrivals and to give them the glad tidings that accommodation, at least temporarily, had been found for them.

The new arrivals were holding a meeting in the third class dining room of the Italian liner, deciding on what their next move would be, when representatives of the local committees came to them with glad tidings and commenced the registration of the new arrivals and the allocation of housing facilities.

Prolonged Formalities

Although the vessel docked at about 2.30 p.m. it was not until after 6 p.m. that the refugees finally got through with various arrangements and were brought to the Customs Jetty, where again a long procedure of passing through Customs examination commenced.

Finally outside, the refugees—men, women and children—were put into trucks together with their light baggage and routed to various parts of the town—Yangtzepoo, Hongkew, the Western area and the French Concession—where, through untiring efforts, the local committee had obtained housing facilities for them.

Well Dressed, But Penniless

Although mostly well-dressed, most of the refugees are understood to be completely penniless and they will be dependent on the community until such time as they find some sort of work.

Aboard the ship they sat mostly huddled together, with the exception of several women with babies in arms and in baby carriages, who sat apart to give the children a chance to sleep. A few young girls and boys ran about the third-class accommodation playing. The others wore serious expressions, not knowing what awaited them in Shanghai.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》。
1938年12月21日

500名犹太
难民
抵达此地

已为从码头
乘卡车接回的群体
准备住所

昨天下午，超过500名来自德国和奥地利的犹太难民乘坐意大利劳埃德·特里埃斯蒂诺轮船公司（Lloyd Triestino）的“比安卡马诺伯爵号”（Conte Biancamano）轮抵达此地。他们是预计不久后将抵达的约3,000至4,000名欧洲移民的先遣队。这些难民中鲜有人会说英语，且妇女和儿童占很大比例。

上海援助欧洲犹太难民委员会的成员，以及过去几个月内抵达上海的众多欧洲犹太人，聚集在上海码头和虹口码头迎接新来者，并告诉他们一个好消息：至少暂时已为他们找到了住所。

当地方委员会的代表带着好消息前来，并开始对新来者进行登记和分配住房设施时，新来者正在意大利邮轮的三等舱餐厅开会，商讨下一步行动。

冗长的手续

虽然该船于下午2点30分左右靠岸，但直到下午6点以后，难民们才最终办完各种手续，被带到海关码头，在那里又开始了漫长的通过海关检查的程序。

最后来到室外，难民们——包括男人、女人和儿童——连同他们的轻便行李一起被装上卡车，并被送往城镇的各个区域——杨树浦、虹口、西区以及法租界——当地委员会通过不懈的努力，已在那里为他们获得了住房设施。

衣着体面，但身无分文

尽管大多衣着体面，但据了解，大多数难民完全身无分文，在找到某种工作之前，他们将依赖社区的援助。

在船上，他们大多挤坐在一起，只有几位怀抱婴儿或推着婴儿车的妇女坐在一旁，以便让孩子们睡觉。少数年轻女孩和男孩在三等舱住宿区跑来跑去玩耍。其他人则表情严肃，不知道在上海等待着他们的是什么。

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。
1939年9月5日

战争局势导致
犹太移民减少

日本驻沪领事、特别董事会四名成员之一的石黑先生（S. Ishiguro）今天上午表示，特别难民移民委员会可能会在一周内举行会议，进一步讨论日本、法国、当地犹太人和工部局当局针对德国犹太人移居上海所制定的法规和措施。这位日本领事官员宣称，由于航运短缺，来自德国的进一步移民将大幅减少，这导致了会议召开的延误。与此同时，目前在上海的许多欧洲犹太难民今天上午继续前往英国领事馆，进行咨询并表示希望服役于英国军队。据官方获悉，目前尚未接纳任何犹太难民，尽管在几起案例中，有关人员被允许留下申请表以备将来参考。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY,
AUG 1 4 1939
Consuls, Shipping Men
Informed Of Decision
By S'hai City Fathers
23372
Town Held Unable To Accommodate Further
Increase; Strain On Municipal
Services Grows Steadily
Refugees En Route Allowed Entrance
No more European Jewish refugees are to be allowed
to enter Shanghai.
This, with the possible exception of refugees already
embarked, is the decision unanimously reached by the
Shanghai Municipal Council.
Letters have already been sent by the SMC to all Con-
sulates, shipping offices and to Mr. Ellis Hayim (for
transmission to all Jewish organizations in Shanghai) giving
the Council's decision.
Done Enough
"Shanghai has already done
enough for the European refugees"
an SMC spokesman told the
Shanghai Evening Post today.
"Do not think, however, that the
SMC is unsympathetic towards
the refugees. Very far from it
But the point has been reached
where Shanghai cannot absorb
any more without a serious strain
upon municipal services.
"And, if the unofficial report
to the effect that the Japanese
authorities are not allowing any
more emigres to settle north of
the Soochow Creek be true, there
is certain no room for them south
of the Creek.
Jewish Societies
"The Council has not done a
large amount financially toward
helping the refugees. The local
Jewish societies have been very
good in their aid to the emigres
while the Council has helped by
granting the use of unoccupied
buildings and land.
"But the sudden arrival of a
large number of refugees has caused
extra work for the Police, who
already have plenty to do. And
an unlimited arrival in a short
period will cause additional strain
on all services. For one instance,
hospitalization is bound to be
needed in increasing magnitude.
Shanghai has done more than its
share already, and it is time for
others to help."
Bad For Emigres
The spokesman also referred to
the fact that their crowding into
a town not prepared for them
would also have a detrimental
effect upon the refugees them-
selves, although the Council
realized that the emigres' attitude
was probably that anything would
be better than the conditions
which they had left.
Emigres who had already em-
barked for Shanghai would not be
turned away, the Council spokes-
man added. On humanitarian
grounds they would be allowed to
enter.
Fifteen Thousand
Jewish refugees from the terror
in Germany and Austria who have
arrived in Shanghai total some
15,000. Another 5000 had been
anticipated before the end of the
year, before the SMC had taken
its decision.
Those who are already on the
way to Shanghai were this morn-
ing estimated at 500. They will
be the last to be permitted in the
International Settlement.
（批：D.S. Pink 8/15 9 80-15k）

1939年8月14日
领事、航运界人士
获知上海市政当局决定
23372
本市被认为无法容纳进一步增加的人口；市政服务压力稳步增长
途中的难民获准入境
不再允许更多的欧洲犹太难民进入上海。
除了可能已经登船的难民外，这是上海公共租界工部局一致达成的决定。
工部局已向所有领事馆、航运办事处以及埃利斯·海姆先生（Ellis Hayim，负责转达给上海所有犹太组织）致函，告知工部局的决定。
做得够多了
“上海已经为欧洲难民做得够多了，”一位工部局发言人今天告诉《上海晚邮报》。“但不要认为工部局对难民缺乏同情心。事实绝非如此。但是，上海已经到了如果不严重加剧市政服务负担就无法再吸收更多人的地步。”
“而且，如果有关日本当局不允许更多移民定居苏州河以北的非官方报道属实，那么苏州河以南肯定也没有他们的容身之地。”
犹太社团
“理事会在财政上为帮助难民所做的并不多。当地犹太社团在援助移民方面表现得非常好，而理事会则通过提供闲置建筑物和土地的使用权来提供帮助。”
“但是，大量难民的突然到来给警察带来了额外的工作，而他们原本就已经事务繁忙。如果在短时间内无限制地涌入，将对所有服务造成额外的压力。例如，住院需求必然会增加。上海已经做得超出了其应尽的本分，现在是其他人提供帮助的时候了。”
对移民不利
该发言人还提到，将他们拥挤在一个未为他们做好准备的城市中，也会对难民自身产生不利影响，尽管理事会意识到移民的态度可能是无论什么条件都比他们离开的地方要好。
工部局发言人补充说，已经登船前往上海的移民不会被拒之门外。出于人道主义理由，他们将获准入境。
一万五千人
逃离德国和奥地利恐怖统治并抵达上海的犹太难民总数约为15,000人。在工部局做出决定之前，曾预计到年底前还将有另外5,000人抵达。
今天早上估计，已经在前往上海途中的难民有500人。他们将是最后一批被允许进入国际租界的人。
（批注：D.S. Pink 8/15 9 80-15k）

Hongkew Jewish Emigres
Curbing Planned

All Jewish refugees arriving in
Shanghai after August 21, will not
be permitted to reside in Hongkew,
according to an official note sent
by the Japanese Naval Landing
Party Headquarters yesterday, to
the committee in charge of Jewish
refugees here. The note pointed
out that even the return of former
Japanese residents is restricted,
apart from the fact that Chinese
are only permitted to return in
small numbers. At the same time,
the note added, a dearth of houses
exists in Hongkew following the
destruction during the 1927 hosti-
lities. These matters, it was stat-
ed, necessitated of additional set-
tlement of Jewish emigres, who at
present total almost one-tenth of
the Japanese community which, a
Japanese spokesman stated, "has
led to a growing fear of friction
arising between the two communi-
ties." Questioned at the Japanese
press conference last evening by
what right the Japanese had adopt-
ed their policy of limiting residence
in areas north of Soochow Creek,
the spokesman replied that por-
tion of the International Settle-
ment was controlled by the Japan-
ese, who could legislate as they
pleased, by reason of military con-
quest.

1939年8月12日

计划限制
虹口犹太移民

根据日本海军陆战队总部昨天发给此处负责犹太难民委员会的一份正式照会，8月21日之后抵达上海的所有犹太难民将不被允许居住在虹口。该照会指出，除了中国人仅被允许少量返回外，甚至前日本居民的返回也受到限制。同时，照会补充说，由于1927年战事期间的破坏，虹口存在房屋短缺问题。据称，这些问题使得必须对犹太移民进行额外的安置安排，目前犹太移民总数几乎占日本侨民社区的十分之一，一位日本发言人称，这“导致了对两个社区之间摩擦日益增加的担忧”。在昨晚的日本记者招待会上，当被问及日本有何权利采取限制苏州河以北地区居住的政策时，该发言人回答说，国际租界的该部分由日本人控制，基于军事征服，他们可以随意立法。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
10449
JUL 3 1930

Emigres Refused
Hungjao Entry

British Arrest Japanese
At Perimeter
Barrier

Reports of tension on the Great
Western Road barrier Saturday
afternoon, when passers-by notic-
ed a certain amount of walla-
walla and a little more conges-
tion than usual, were finally trac-
ed to the arrest by the British
military of a Japanese gendarme
in plain-clothes, and the preven-
tion of a party of Jewish emigre
children from going to the fresh-
air camp arranged for them. Both
affairs have now been settled.

Misunderstanding is the reason
given for both affairs. As re-
gards the 50 emigre children, col-
lected with a great amount of
work and running around, it
transpired that their Japanese
consular pass had not been coun-
tersigned by the military in con-
trol of the Hungjao Area, and
that they had to have the same
authority for residing there as do
normal residents.

In Plain Clothes

The gardarme episode took
place after the man and a con-
frere had arrived at the barrier,
going in the direction of Hungjao.
Their ricshas halted on the Bri-
tish side, out of the way, and one
of the gendarmes walked along
to go to the Lincoln Avenue mili-
tary headquarters. The other, in
plain clothes, stayed and chatted
with the Japanese sentries.

When the gendarme saw his
confrere returning, he walked
into the middle of the road in
front of the British sentry and
called the ricshas. As he was in
the way of traffic, the sentry
asked and motioned to him to
move. When the latter did not
do this, a British sergeant came
up and spoke to him. The Ja-
panese paid absolutely no atten-
tion to the British sergeant, who
then tapped the gendarme on the
shoulder.

Japanese Released

Losing his temper, the gendarme
swung around and tapped the
British sergeant on the chest,
whereupon the British guard im-
mediately arrested the gendarme.
Half an hour later, with the
gendarme's identity established,
he was released.

The emigre children, greatly
disappointed, had to be taken
home again. The military autho-
risation, however, has now been
obtained, and the camps will be
able to function as arranged.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》。
10449
1930年7月3日

移民被拒
进入虹桥

英国人在外围
屏障逮捕日本人

周六下午，大西路（Great Western Road）屏障处出现紧张局势的报道，当时路人注意到有一些喧哗（walla-walla）和比平时稍多的拥堵，最终查明原因是英国军方逮捕了一名便衣日本宪兵，并阻止一群犹太移民儿童前往为他们安排的呼吸新鲜空气的营地。这两件事现已解决。

误解是这两件事给出的原因。关于那50名经过大量工作和奔波才聚集起来的移民儿童，事实证明，他们的日本领事通行证未经控制虹桥地区的军方副署，并且他们必须拥有与正常居民相同的在该地区居住的授权。

身着便衣

宪兵事件发生在该男子和一名同伴到达屏障，朝虹桥方向行进之后。他们的黄包车停在英国一侧的路边，其中一名宪兵步行前往林肯大道（Lincoln Avenue）的军事总部。另一名身着便衣的宪兵留下来与日本哨兵聊天。

当这名宪兵看到他的同伴返回时，他走到英国哨兵前面的马路中间，呼唤黄包车。由于他阻碍了交通，哨兵要求并示意他让开。当后者没有这样做时，一名英国军士走上前与他交谈。该日本人完全不理会英国军士，军士随后拍了拍宪兵的肩膀。

日本人获释

宪兵发脾气，转身拍了拍英国军士的胸口，随即英国卫兵立即逮捕了该宪兵。半小时后，在确认了宪兵的身份后，他被释放。

移民儿童非常失望，不得不再次被送回家。不过，现在已经获得了军事授权，营地能够按计划运作。

BIERGARTEN IM

European Emigre Cafe
Provides Unusual Note
In Shanghai Of Today
Continental Open-Air Layout Shows Touches
Of Homeland To Jewish Refugees; Handy
Meeting Places Prove Popular
Walls Adorned By Advertising Cards
By T. A. BUTLER
UPROOTED from their foundations in the heart of their
native land by a cyclone of political strife, thousands of
German and Austrian refugees have been tossed along by the
storm over half the distance of the globe, coming to earth in
of all places, a tiny patch of territory in Shanghai north of
Soochow Creek.
The Broadway-Wayside district presents an unusual ap-
pearance these days. It is as if a portion of Europe had been
transplanted intact to the shores of the muddy Whangpoo.
Mingled with the war-torn ruins of earlier days in the vicinity,
a new community has been born, timidly, but ever-increasingly,
spreading out among the demolished buildings and scrubby
vacant lots of wayside.
Cafes Spring Up
Those delightful little German cafes and beer taverns have
sprung up like mushrooms in the district, lending to it an air
of mild gaiety that was not evident, even in the palmier days
of the district. The old blood and thunder bars and cabarets of
earlier and more rousing days have given way to the quiet cafes
and beer halls which are more in keeping with the present
inhabitants of the place.
Everywhere there is a wide stretch of sidewalk available
outside a cafe, that stretch has been converted into a sidewalk
garden where the good people may take their ease on a warm
summer's night amid the potted plants and flowers which lend
a pastoral air to the scene. Hard as their lot may be, these
refugees manage to entertain themselves by pleasant discourse
and a few glasses of beer in the company of bosom companions
Beginning to Smile
YES, these emigres are beginning to smile again. Although
talk is still somewhat guarded, and the old dread
is hard to shake off, the people are gradually beginning to
come out of their shells and breathe the air of freedom
again. They are certainly unmolested across the creek and
appear to be on very friendly terms with the Japanese.
Take a glance inside one of these little beer taverns. Walk in
and order a glass of beer and then just sit there and take in
what goes on around you. You'll probably notice, in fact you
can't help but notice, the walls plastered with home-made signs
which the proprietor of the place has allowed to be put up
there by fellow emigres.
Various Services
These signs announce to all and sundry that, for the mere
asking, there is to be had the services of a dentist, carpenter,
manicurist, pedicurist or what have you. Another sign states
that one family wishes to share its modest lodgings with a
compatriot for the sake of economy. It's good advertising, and
it costs nothing.
In the rear of the tavern you can hear the incessant tink-
ling of an old piano. Where's it coming from? It's just another
refugee playing the piano for his food and lodging, just enough
to keep him going until he finds something to do. Quite a few
of the emigres are musicians and they have brought with them
all the exquisite melodies of the continent.
A.S.
Pulk
(4)

1939年6月30日
BIERGARTEN IM
电报挂号：
总裁
总经理
司库
编辑
关于J
ese基督徒的报告
在s处叙述
Rev. Mr.
我们不在
欧洲流亡者咖啡馆
为今日的上海
增添不寻常的情调
大陆式露天布局向犹太难民
展示了祖国的风情；便利的
聚会场所颇受欢迎
墙壁上装饰着广告卡片
T. A. BUTLER 撰

被政治斗争的旋风从祖国腹地的根基中连根拔起，成千上万的德国和奥地利难民被风暴抛掷，跨越了半个地球的距离，最终落脚于——在所有地方中偏偏是——苏州河以北上海的一小块领土上。

如今，百老汇-韦斯特（Broadway-Wayside）地区呈现出一种不寻常的景象。仿佛欧洲的一部分被完整地移植到了浑浊的黄浦江畔。与该地区早期战火摧残后的废墟交织在一起，一个新的社区诞生了，它怯生生地、但日益扩展地分布在路边被拆除的建筑和杂草丛生的空地之间。

咖啡馆涌现

那些令人愉悦的德式小咖啡馆和啤酒馆在该地区如雨后春笋般涌现，赋予该地区一种温和的欢乐气氛，这即使在该地区较繁荣的日子里也不曾显现。早期更为喧闹日子里那些充满血腥与暴力的酒吧和歌舞厅，已让位于更符合此地当前居民口味的安静咖啡馆和啤酒馆。

在任何一家咖啡馆外，只要有一大片可用的人行道，那片区域就被改造成人行道花园，善良的人们可以在温暖的夏夜，在盆栽植物和鲜花之间悠闲自得，这些植物为场景增添了一种田园气息。尽管他们的命运艰难，这些难民仍通过与知心同伴愉快地交谈和喝几杯啤酒来娱乐自己。

开始微笑

是的，这些流亡者又开始微笑了。虽然谈话仍然有些谨慎，旧的恐惧难以摆脱，但人们正逐渐走出封闭的状态，再次呼吸自由的空气。他们在河对岸确实未受骚扰，并且似乎与日本人保持着非常友好的关系。

瞥一眼这些小啤酒馆的内部。走进去，点一杯啤酒，然后坐在那里，观察周围发生的一切。你很可能会注意到，事实上你不可能不注意到，墙上贴满了自制的标语，这是店主允许其他流亡同胞张贴在那里的。

各种服务

这些标语向所有人宣告，只要开口询问，就可以获得牙医、木匠、美甲师、修脚师或其他任何人的服务。另一则标语声明，为了节约起见，一个家庭希望与一位同胞分享其简陋的住所。这是很好的广告，而且无需花费分文。

在酒馆的后部，你可以听到一架旧钢琴不断的叮当声。声音从哪里来？这只是另一位难民为了换取食宿而弹奏钢琴，勉强维持生计，直到他找到事情可做。相当多的流亡者是音乐家，他们带来了大陆上所有优美的旋律。

A.S.
Pulk
(4)

pages.en:
19349

Beer Garden
FINISHED your beer? Well, just saunter across the street
and take in that quaint beer garden. It's not really a garden
it's just a wide place in the street, but with the addition of a
few large umbrellas to protect patrons from the scorching rays
of the sun, and a few potted plants and shrubs, it takes on the
appearance of a real honest-to-goodness garden. Here, seated
in the wicker chairs, the troubled "chosen people sit for hours
and discuss their future, always the future, the past is buried
and is brought to light only in dark nightmares.
If it's a roof garden you're looking for, you won't have to
go far. Stroll along the quiet street until you come to a theatre.
Walk up to the roof of the building—there is no elevator—and
you'll find a delightful garden with a polished slab in the
center for dancing and lined with tables and chairs. Here again
potted plants and shrubs are very much in evidence, and up
here the breeze has a wonderful cooling effect.
Few Dancers
Although there is a small, and very good, orchestra in the
place, few of the customers indulge in dancing. The majority of
them having been walking around Shanghai all day, ever in
the hope of some good prospect, are content to take it easy
with a cold one or two, listening to the music and enjoy-
ing the gentle, cooling breeze.
The waitresses are all nice clean-looking German girls,
speaking but little English, and serving customers with a shy
attitude. Most of them, however, are rapidly picking up Eng-
lish expressions. Anyway, just ask for "beer" and you'll get it.
Interesting Panorama
A VIEW from this roof garden of the surrounding streets
below reveals an interesting panorama of life. Most of
the people sit out-doors on stools or door-steps chatting in the
quiet summer evening. A friend strolls by and he is invited into
the circle with much hailing of delight and good fellowship.
Kiddies run around playing on the streets or scamper over
vacant lots, cluttered with the ravages of war.
Dogs are by no means in the minority in the new colony.
Even though it is pretty tough sledding, well you can always
find enough to feed faithful Fido.
Unlike Orient
All in all, the neighborhood is strangely unlike any other
part of Shanghai. It seems to be remotely apart from the
Orient, it is as it were a part of Europe that had been establish-
ed for hundreds of years.
These people have just moved in, and with quiet courage
and hard work, set about building themselves a home in the
new land, asking only peace and to be allowed to live their own
lives.
pages.zh:
19349

啤酒花园

喝完啤酒了吗？好吧，只需漫步穿过街道，去看看那个别致的啤酒花园。它其实并不是一个花园，只是街道上的一块宽阔地带，但加上几把大伞以保护顾客免受烈日的炙烤，再加上一些盆栽植物和灌木，它就呈现出一个真正的、货真价实的花园的模样。在这里，坐在藤椅上，忧心忡忡的“选民”们一坐就是几个小时，讨论着他们的未来，总是未来，过去已被埋葬，只有在黑暗的噩梦中才会重现。

如果你在寻找屋顶花园，你不必走远。沿着安静的街道漫步，直到来到一家剧院。走上建筑物的屋顶——那里没有电梯——你会发现一个迷人的花园，中央有一块抛光石板用于跳舞，周围排列着桌椅。这里同样随处可见盆栽植物和灌木，而且在这里，微风具有奇妙的降温效果。

舞者寥寥

虽然那里有一个小型且非常优秀的管弦乐队，但很少有顾客 indulge in dancing（纵情舞蹈）。他们中的大多数人整天在上海四处奔波，一直希望能有好的前景，因此满足于喝着冷啤酒，听着音乐，享受轻柔凉爽的微风。

女服务员都是看起来干净整洁的德国女孩，只会说很少的英语，以害羞的态度为顾客服务。然而，她们中的大多数人正在迅速掌握英语表达。无论如何，只要说要“beer”（啤酒），你就会得到它。

有趣的全景

从这个屋顶花园俯瞰周围的街道，展现出一幅有趣的生活全景图。大多数人坐在户外的凳子上或门阶上，在宁静的夏夜聊天。一位朋友漫步经过，伴随着欢快的欢呼和友好的情谊，他被邀请加入圈子。孩子们在街上玩耍奔跑，或在杂乱不堪、布满战争创伤的空地上窜来窜去。

在这个新殖民地中，狗绝非少数。尽管生活相当艰难，但你总能找到足够的食物来喂养忠诚的菲多（Fido，指狗）。

不同于东方

总而言之，这个街区奇怪地不像上海的任何其他地区。它似乎与东方遥不可及，仿佛是一个已经建立了数百年的欧洲部分。

这些人刚刚搬进来，带着安静的勇气和辛勤的工作，着手在这片新土地上为自己建立家园，只要求和平，并被允许过自己的生活。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
JUN 26 1939

A New Homeland In China
A SPECTACULAR plan for settling foreign emigrants in interior China, chiefly Yunnan province, has been announced here. It is known that the National Government has for some time been exploring the possibilities of such a scheme, though the precise number of emigrants has not been previously mentioned, and endorsement of the idea has been forthcoming from a number of quarters including this newspaper. The scheme would provide for 100,000 emigrees but it should be noted that Chungking holds this to be too great a number, and sets the total more cautiously at 10,000.
J. Berglas, described as a German industrialist, has announced that the plan provides for the settling in China of emigrants from any part of the world irrespective of nationality, creed or political affiliations—though it seems obvious that Central European Jews are the most logical class to respond to this offer and Shanghai is affording more or less precarious shelter to more than 10,000 of these already. It would be provided that these must furnish finances sufficient to cover their food and shelter over a period of about a year. They would be granted the same rights of residence, work and governmental protection as the Chinese, while accepting correspondingly the same responsibilities as Chinese.
Communal in nature, the scheme includes provision for a co-operative banking institution. A committee of all presidents of emigration committees throughout the world would supervise the working of the plan and they would be held responsible for the intellectual advancement of the emigrants and their preparation for a new life in China.
Funds, it is felt, should be forthcoming from many friends of refugees who are at present under relatively small but continuing charges and who might be willing to provide a lump sum if this brought assurance of self-respecting and self-sustaining place in the world for those whom they seek to help. It is locally reported that the German Government views the plan favorably, while the Chinese Government is anxious to acquire trained foreigners, particularly, to develop rich western territories not previously exploited.
The plan does not impress us as impossibly Utopian and we hope there may be in it some fresh opportunity for unfortunate people deserving far better from the world than they are getting at present.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》。
1939年6月26日

在中国的新家园

一项将外国移民安置在中国内地（主要是云南省）的宏伟计划在此宣布。据悉，国民政府一段时间以来一直在探索此类方案的可能性，尽管此前并未提及移民的确切人数，且包括本报在内的多方已对该想法表示支持。该计划拟安置10万名流亡者，但应注意，重庆方面认为这一数字过大，更为谨慎地将总数定为1万人。

J. Berglas，被描述为一位德国工业家，宣布该计划规定安置来自世界任何地方的移民，不分国籍、信仰或政治派别——尽管显然中欧犹太人是最有可能响应此提议的群体，而上海已经为超过1万名此类人员提供了或多或少不稳定的庇护。条件是他们必须提供足以支付约一年期间食物和住所的资金。他们将享有与中国公民相同的居住、工作和政府保护权利，同时相应地承担与中国公民相同的责任。

该计划具有公社性质，包括设立合作银行机构的规定。由世界各地移民委员会主席组成的委员会将监督计划的实施，并负责移民的智力提升以及为他们在中国的新生活做准备。

据认为，资金应来自许多难民之友，这些人目前承担着相对较小但持续的费用，如果这笔一次性捐款能为他们所帮助的那些人带来在这个世界上自尊和自给自足的地位的保证，他们可能愿意提供。据本地报道，德国政府对该计划持赞成态度，而中国政府渴望获得受过训练的外国人，特别是为了开发以前未开发的富饶西部领土。

该计划给我们留下的印象并非不可能实现的乌托邦，我们希望其中能为不幸的人们提供一些新的机会，他们从这个世界得到的待遇远不如他们应得的那么好。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
MAY 1 7 1939
Jewish Visitors Caught
In Nippon “Spy” Trap
Victims of the Japanese spy
craze, which has extended even
to schoolboys in Japan, two
German-Jewish refugees were
nabbed by the Yokohama water
police, when two Japanese secon-
dary-school students accused them
of being international spies, ac-
cording to reports received here.
The couple, Mr. and Mrs. Max
Schoeffer, were third class pas-
sengers on the Tatuta Maru and
were taking pictures of the Yoko-
suka fortified zone from the deck
of the ship when they were
observed by the schoolboys. The
youths, Yukio Sukeharu and
Isamu Saito, were returning from
a holiday in the Kwansai. When
they came upon the couple snap-
ping the forbidden pictures in
Yokohama harbor, they made
known to the refugees that they
would like to have their pictures
taken also.
To oblige the lads the couple
took their pictures and thought
no more of the matter. Upon ar-
rival at Yokohama, the two boys
scooted off the ship and inform-
ed the water police that there
were a couple of spies aboard the
liner who had been snapping
pictures, saying that the roll of
film could be identified because it
contained their pictures also.
The zealous police lost no time
in taking the bewildered couple
into custody and commence to
question them. Upon finding out
that they were unable to under-
stand the signs prohibiting the
practice of photography in Yoko-
nama harbor, the police released
the refugees, at the same time
cautioning them against any
further attempts at picture snap-
ping.
The youths were warmly re-
commended for their alertness,
and the Japanese authorities are
happy that their public is on
guard against alien activities, the
report concludes.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》。
1939年5月17日
犹太访客落入
日本“间谍”陷阱

据此处收到的报告称，作为日本间谍狂热（甚至波及到日本学童）的受害者，两名德裔犹太难民被横滨水上警察逮捕，起因是两名日本中学生指控他们是国际间谍。

这对夫妇，Max Schoeffer先生和夫人，是“龙田丸”（Tatuta Maru）号的三等舱乘客，当他们在船甲板上拍摄横须贺要塞区时，被学生们观察到。这两名青年，Yukio Sukeharu和Isamu Saito，刚从关西度假归来。当他们在横滨港遇到这对夫妇拍摄禁止拍摄的照片时，他们向难民表示，也希望让他们给自己拍照。

为了成全这两个孩子，这对夫妇给他们拍了照，此后便不再多想。抵达横滨后，两个男孩匆匆下船，告知水上警察，邮轮上有一对间谍一直在拍照，并称胶卷可以辨认，因为里面也包含了他们的照片。

热情的警察毫不迟疑地将这对困惑的夫妇拘留并开始审问。在发现他们无法理解横滨港禁止摄影的标志后，警察释放了难民，同时警告他们不得再尝试拍照。

报告最后总结道，这两名青年的警觉性受到了热烈推荐，日本当局很高兴公众对外国人的活动保持警惕。

1939年4月17日
C.230

犹太难民造成的经济威胁

来自欧洲的移民
即将构成外籍人口的四分之一

上海在试图突然吸收大量难民时面临严峻问题；俄国人的涌入历时15年

只有小部分人在本市找到工作

作者：约翰·阿勒斯（John Ahlers）

关于在上海的德国犹太难民的经济问题，人们经常从难民的立场进行审视。然而，还有一个角度尚待考虑，即从上海面对难民涌入这一视角出发。

自去年秋季以来，已有6000多名德国犹太人抵达上海。下个月预计还将有约3000人抵沪。不到六周的时间内，此地的犹太难民总数将达到约10,000人，而且就这些上海居民而言，还有更多人计划前来上海。对于定期往返上海的德国、意大利和日本轮船来说，这种增加是实质性的，引发了一系列新的严重问题。在这些国家的船只上，可以用德国货币支付船票，许多月份的舱位已被预订至满员。目前希望移民上海的德国犹太人发现，即使提前到九月份也很难订到舱位。对舱位的需求如此强烈，以至于在德国似乎出现了一种倒卖船票的勾当，一些投机者预先锁定大量船票，并以高额溢价出售给移民。

严峻的问题

上海是一座拥有数百万人口的世界大城市。从远处看，上海居民人数增加1000、10,000甚至更多来自德国的难民，似乎无关紧要。然而事实上，对于黄浦江畔的这座城市来说，10,000名德国犹太人的迁入构成的问题，比对于巴黎、伦敦或纽约等城市要严重得多，而这些城市都在拼命努力阻止这些难民进入。德国难民不能、也不打算被计入上海数百万中国居民的平均数中。难民是对上海西方各国侨民社区的补充，

（批注：1/4）

pages.en:
War Losses
While a series of large enterprises as well as of individuals managed to secure extraordinary war profits, the bulk of the western residents here sustained losses during the war. It appears to be not known in Europe that the outlook for western business in Shanghai has deteriorated so much that there is a definite trend towards emigration from Shanghai. A considerable number of small and medium western firms which prior to the war did a thriving business in Shanghai, have since closed down and transferred their activities to Hongkong, Singapore, Manila, and to a minor extent to Dairen.
In most of the remaining western firms and enterprises, there is no tendency to enlarge the staff and to expand, but a continuous trend toward restriction to save overhead expenses.
It is in this situation, that the German Jewish refugees arrive here by the thousands. They are well-known as active, industrious and thrifty people, but there is no indication that their business capacity is remarkably surpassing that of the average white businessmen in Shanghai, let alone the Chinese. In these circumstances, it is difficult to see how the bulk of the Jewish emigrants will be able to establish and maintain themselves here.
Quite a number of the Jewish refugees did not arrive here penniless, but carried with them some capital which they managed to export in various ways and forms from Germany, or to mobilize with the assistance of relatives or friends in other European countries. In some individual cases, these capital funds seem to be considerable, and among the newcomers are a few really rich Jews.

Foreign Capital
This import of capital, however important in individual cases it may be, is not likely to matter as regards the supply of Shanghai with western capital. There are over $200,000,000 of foreign money invested in Shanghai, while the aggregate capital funds of the rich among the newly arrived refugees are certainly far below a petty $1,000,000. This import of capital is of importance only to those concerned.
The few wealthy Jews coming to Shanghai will find here possibilities of investment. Shanghai, it is true, has an over-supply of banks and commercial firms, but there is still an open field for a series of new industrial enterprises, producing modern commodities which thus far have been imported but which could be manufactured locally.
pages.zh:
战争损失

虽然一系列大型企业以及个人设法获得了惊人的战争利润，但此地大多数西方居民在战争期间遭受了损失。欧洲方面似乎并不知晓，上海西方商业的前景已恶化到如此地步，以至于出现了明确的从上海移居国外的趋势。相当数量的中小型西方公司在战前于上海生意兴隆，此后已关闭并将业务转移至香港、新加坡、马尼拉，少数转移至大连。

在大多数剩余的西方公司和企业中，没有扩大员工队伍和扩张业务的倾向，而是持续趋向于紧缩以节省日常开支。

正是在这种情况下，成千上万的德国犹太难民抵达此地。他们以活跃、勤劳和节俭著称，但没有迹象表明他们的商业能力显著超过上海一般的西方商人，更不用说中国人了。在这种情况下，很难看出大多数犹太移民如何能在此立足并维持生计。

不少犹太难民并非身无分文地来到这里，而是携带了一些资本，他们通过各种方式和形式设法从德国输出这些资本，或在其他欧洲国家亲友的帮助下调动资金。在某些个别案例中，这些资金数额似乎相当可观，新来者中也有少数真正富有的犹太人。

外来资本

然而，无论这种资本输入在个别情况下多么重要，它不太可能影响上海的西方资本供应。上海的外国投资超过2亿美元，而新近抵达的富裕难民的资金总额肯定远低于微不足道的100万美元。这种资本输入仅对相关人士具有重要意义。

少数来到上海的富有犹太人将在这里找到投资机会。诚然，上海的银行和商业公司供过于求，但仍有一系列新的工业企业领域有待开发，生产迄今为止依赖进口但可在本地制造的现代商品。

pages.en:
Professional Men
In such enterprises, another
number of refugees without capi-
tal but with specialized profes-
sional knowledge and experience,
such as engineers, technicians, etc.
could certainly find a lasting
position. Also a series of existing
industrial plants in Shanghai pro-
bably would like to engage, and
occasionally have engaged, such
specialists from among the re-
fugees. There still appears, more-
over, to be room in Shanghai for
the establishment of a certain
number of professional men from
the German refugees such as me-
dical doctors, lawyers, and educa-
tors, provided these men are of a
really high professional standing
and dispose of valuable experience
and knowledge which, here and
there, may be still lacking in
Shanghai. There are yet some
other occasional opportunities out
of which refugees may make a
living by availing themselves of
exceptionally good experience, con-
nections and ingenuity.
But 10,000 refugees will need,
discounting married women and
children, about 5000 jobs. It would
be preposterous to allege that there
are in Shanghai, fit and open for
white men, about 5000 jobs which
had not been discovered before the
arrival of the refugees. A deter-
mined effort may disclose a few
hundreds of such new jobs, but
by no means 5000.
Lucky Ones
Up to the present, efforts of the
committees looking after the re-
fugees, and of those German Jews
who take care of themselves, have
resulted in the employment or
establishment in business of little
more than 1000 refugees here,
taking into account the women
and children of the individuals
concerned. More than 5000 re-
fugees, however, have not yet
found anything to make their
living, and more than 3000 of
these are entirely penniless and
depend for food and shelter on
charity.
In the sight of the 5000 needy
refugees the achievement of pro-
viding a living for the 1000 others
may not look a great accomplish-
ment. It may look still less so
because many of the jobs hastily
found or arranged for the new-
comers are obviously temporary and
transitional jobs. But hats have
to be taken off to the refugee
committees when we think of the
limited capacity of Shanghai to
digest newcomers, and in parti-
cular refugees. In past years,
times of boom and of depression
taken together, Shanghai allowed
for an annual new establishment
of western newcomers here to the
average amount of about 2000. At
this rate, the former Russian re-
fugees have been digested in
Shanghai.
pages.zh:
专业人士

在这样的企业中，另一批没有资本但拥有专门专业知识和经验的难民，如工程师、技术人员等，肯定能找到长期的职位。此外，上海现有的一系列工厂可能愿意，并且偶尔确实雇佣了难民中的此类专家。此外，上海似乎仍有空间容纳一定数量的德国难民中的专业人士，如医生、律师和教育家，前提是这些人具有真正高的专业地位，并拥有宝贵的经验和知识，而这些在上海某些地方可能仍然缺乏。还有一些其他零星的机会，难民可以利用其特别良好的经验、关系和聪明才智从中谋生。

但是，除去已婚妇女和儿童，10,000名难民需要大约5000个工作岗位。声称上海有大约5000个适合西方人且尚未被发现的工作岗位，这在难民到来之前是不存在的，这种说法是荒谬的。经过坚决的努力可能会揭示出几百个这样的新工作岗位，但绝不会有5000个。

幸运儿

截至目前，照顾难民的委员会以及那些自谋生路的德国犹太人的努力，结果是此地仅有1000多名难民获得就业或建立业务，这还包括相关人员的妇女和儿童。然而，超过5000名难民尚未找到任何谋生之道，其中3000多人完全身无分文，依靠慈善救济获取食物和住所。

在5000名贫困难民看来，为另外1000人提供生计的成就可能算不上伟大的功绩。考虑到为新来者匆忙找到或安排的工作很多显然是临时性和过渡性的，这一成就看起来更是微不足道。但是，当我们想到上海吸收新来者，特别是难民的能力有限时，不得不向难民委员会致敬。在过去几年里，无论是繁荣时期还是萧条时期，上海每年平均允许约2000名西方新来者在此定居。按照这个速度，此前的俄国难民已被上海所吸收。

pages.en:
Russian Arrival
Naturally, confronted with the
problem of the German refugees,
Shanghailanders first think of the
Russian refugees. There are, it
is true, substantial differences in
character and circumstances of
the present Jewish immigration
from Germany as compared with
the coming of the White Russians,
but there are many more similari-
ties between these two immigra-
tions than between the case of
the German Jews and the settle-
ment here of the other western-
ers. Shanghai has digested more
than 20,000 Russians. These Rus-
sians, however, arrived here
gradually and the process of their
digestion lasted over 15 years.
A great many of these Russians
have established themselves in
good and comfortable positions, or
have founded prosperous enter-
prises. Nevertheless, there is still
a great deal of appalling poverty
in the local Russian community.
Many Russians continue to be
living just on the edge of the
so-called existence minimum, lucky
when they can earn in exchange
for heavy work those $70 monthly,
which, in the beginning of the
Jewish immigration from Ger-
many, many German refugees got
here gratuitously out of charity
funds. The average standard of
income in the local Russian com-
munity is lower than in either
the American, British, German,
or French communities, and the
arrival of tens of thousands of
Russians has definitely lowered
the general average living stan-
dard of westerners here.
Chances Diminish
In these circumstances, it will
obviously take several years for
Shanghai to digest those 5000
Jewish emigrants who have al-
ready arrived here and who, thus
far, have looked in vain for a job.
The further influx, in the near
future, of thousands more of
German Jews is not justified by
the actual possibilities for such
emigrants to make a living here.
Their arrival is likely to diminish
the chances of the more recent
newcomers, and to delay their
digestion by Shanghai. A great
many of the prospective further
Jewish emigrants do not possess
any funds, and the committees
taking care of them recently an-
nounced that they will be out of
funds within three weeks. It is
starvation, and not establishment,
which is lying ahead of the bulk
of future emigrants from Germany
in Shanghai.
The Jewish mass emigration
doubtless constitutes a serious
menace to part of the established
western communities as well as to
certain classes of the Chinese in
Shanghai. Shop-keeping, restau-
rant and coffee-house business,
tailoring and dress-making, and
beauty-parloring are attracting
many of the emigrants. Many
others are on the outlook for or-
dinary clerkships in all sorts of
offices, or for occupation as sales-
men, tutors, musicians, physical
instructors, etc. In all these
branches of business activities,
Shanghai appears to have had,
even before the arrival of the
German emigrants, a definite over-
supply. Although there may be
many exceptions allowing a new-
comer to establish himself with-
out depriving an older Shanghai-
lander of his business or position,
it cannot be doubted that the
chief effort of the refugees is,
and is destined to remain, a com-
petitive one as regards many
established interests in Shanghai.
pages.zh:
俄国人的到来

自然，面对德国难民的问题，上海老外侨首先想到的是俄国难民。诚然，目前来自德国的犹太移民与白俄人的到来在性质和环境上存在实质性差异，但这两次移民之间的相似之处，远多于德国犹太人与其他西方人在此定居情况之间的相似之处。上海已吸收了20,000多名俄国人。然而，这些俄国人是逐渐抵达的，吸收过程持续了15年以上。许多俄国人已经确立了良好和舒适的地位，或创办了繁荣的企业。尽管如此，当地俄国社区中仍然存在大量的惊人贫困。许多俄国人继续生活在所谓的最低生存线边缘，如果能通过繁重劳动每月赚取70美元，就算幸运了，而在德国犹太移民初期，许多德国难民是从慈善基金中免费获得这笔钱的。当地俄国社区的平均收入水平低于美国、英国、德国或法国社区，数以万计俄国人的到来确实降低了此地西方人的整体平均生活水平。

机会减少

在这种情况下，上海显然需要数年时间才能消化那5000名已经抵达此地且迄今求职无果的犹太移民。近期数千名德国犹太人的进一步涌入，并没有基于此类移民在此谋生的实际可能性作为依据。他们的到来可能会减少较新来者的机会，并延缓上海对他们的吸收。许多预期的后续犹太移民没有任何资金，照顾他们的委员会最近宣布，他们的资金将在三周内耗尽。等待大多数未来从德国来沪移民的不是定居立业，而是饥饿。

犹太人大规模移民无疑对上海部分既定的西方社区以及某些阶层的中国人构成了严重威胁。零售店、餐馆和咖啡馆业务、裁缝和服装制作以及美容行业吸引了许多移民。许多人还在寻找各类办公室的普通职员职位，或担任销售员、家庭教师、音乐家、体育教练等职业。在所有这些商业活动领域，甚至在德国移民到来之前，上海似乎就已经存在明显的供过于求。虽然可能有许多例外情况，允许新来者在不妨碍老上海外侨的业务或职位的情况下立足，但毫无疑问，难民的主要努力方向，并且注定将继续保持，是与上海许多既定利益进行竞争。

pages.en:
Community Structure
The very structure of the
British, American, French, Italian
and German communities in
Shanghai is such that the large
majority of their members have
little reason to feel anxiety over
economic competition on the part
of the German Jewish emigrants.
The same may be said of most
of the local residents who are
citizens of the minor European
states. It is chiefly the medium
and lower strata of the Russian
community, and the modernized
Chinese middle class in Shanghai
who will have to cope with he
economic competition of the new
comers from Germany. Shanghai
has always been, and still is, a
broad-minded city inspired with
a far-going liberalism which will
allow for all sorts of normal com-
petition in business. There can
be no objection against a Jewish
emigrant opening a shop which
may damage or ruin an older
established business, or against a
Jewish office-worker endeavoring
to obtain employment here Effi-
ciency must rank first.
As a matter of course, however,
it has to be insisted that the
economic competition of the Ger-
man Jews with older Shanghai-
landers be a normal one, and
abide by the rules. While there
is no anti-Jewish discrimination
in Shanghai, there ought not to
develop anything like a pro-
Jewish discrimination. It would
be an appalling injustice if
established Shanghailanders were
forced out of business and em-
ployment merely to make place for
the new emigrants from Germany.
It appears that in certain, for-
tunately still limited, instances
definitely objectionable practices
have been developed in favor of
or by the new emigrants. It seems
that in some cases, Russians and
Chinese have been, or are going
to be, deprived of jobs which were
or will be turned over to some of
the newcomers. It is also strict-
ly objectionable that new em-
igrants offer to work, for a certain
time, without payment in offices
where they hope to oust sooner
or later, one or the other of the
established employees. It is in the
interest of the Jewish emigrants
themselves that such practices
should be discontinued immediate-
ly in order not to create anti-
Jewish feeling in Shanghai.
pages.zh:
社区结构
上海英国、美国、法国、意大利和德国侨民群体的结构本身决定了，其绝大多数成员几乎没有理由对德籍犹太移民带来的经济竞争感到焦虑。大多数身为小欧洲国家公民的本地居民也是如此。主要必须应对来自德国新移民经济竞争的，是俄国侨民群体的中下层以及上海现代化的中国中产阶级。上海一直是一座胸怀宽广的城市，深受深远自由主义精神的鼓舞，允许各种正常的商业竞争。对于犹太移民开设可能损害或摧毁老牌商号的店铺，或者犹太职员努力在此谋求职位，无人可以反对。效率必须居于首位。

当然，必须坚持的一点是，德籍犹太人与老上海人之间的经济竞争必须是正常的，并遵守规则。虽然上海不存在反犹歧视，但也不应出现任何形式的亲犹歧视。如果仅仅为了给来自德国的新移民腾出空间，而迫使老上海人失去生意和工作，那将是一种可怕的不公。看来在某些情况下——幸运的是目前仍有限——已经出现了明显令人反感的、有利于或由新移民实施的做法。似乎在有些案例中，俄国人和华人已经或即将被剥夺工作，而这些工作已被或将被转交给部分新移民。同样严格令人反感的是，新移民提出在一段时间内无偿工作，以期迟早排挤掉某位在职员工。为了不在上海引发反犹情绪，立即停止此类做法符合犹太移民自身的利益。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
MAR 1 4 1939

What Do You Think?
The Refugee Problem
(Israel's Messenger)
THE RANKS of the Shanghai Jewish Community continue to swell as every month new batches of refugees continue to arrive in Shanghai. Reuter's report that 1000 additional Jewish refugees are already on the way to Shanghai on the Conte Biancamano has cause alarm mong a section of the international community, and the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury has advocated in a leading article the complete stoppage of further immigration on account of what it terms the "alarmingly growing problem." This same journal has appealed to the local Consular Body to convene an extraordinary meeting in order to cope with the danger which has become "almost terrifying." There are many angles from which to view the Refugee problem and taking all in all, we fail to appreciate the Evening Post's warning that a severe crisis will ensue unless something is done to shut tight the doors of Shanghai to further batches of people coming in.
On humanitarian grounds alone, the cries of suffering and pain must not go unanswered. The local Refugee Committees and Shanghai Jewry have nobly risen to the occasion by extending a helping hand to everyone in need of aid. It is within our power to help mend the broken lives of our co-religionists, and in order to do so, no efforts must be spared in the right direction. Therein lies the crux of the refugee problem.
Homer Martin says it is true that Reds bore into labor unions. Their number is overemphasized, he reports, but not their ability as bores.
Five years repeal in America finds drinking definitely on the decline. Americans may yet become a sober people if prohibitionists and prosperity will stay away from their door.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》
1939年3月14日

你怎么看？
难民问题
（《以色列信使报》）
随着每月新一批难民持续抵达上海，上海犹太社区的队伍不断壮大。路透社报道另有1000名犹太难民正乘“比安卡马诺伯爵号”（Conte Biancamano）轮前来上海，这在部分国际社群中引起了恐慌，《上海晚邮报与水星报》在一篇社论中主张完全停止进一步移民，理由是其所称的“惊人增长的问题”。该报还呼吁当地领事团召开特别会议，以应对这一已变得“几乎令人恐惧”的危险。看待难民问题有许多角度，总体而言，我们无法认同《晚邮报》的警告，即除非采取某种措施紧紧关闭上海大门以阻挡后续人群进入，否则将爆发严重危机。

仅就人道主义立场而言，受苦与痛苦的呼号不应得不到回应。当地难民委员会和上海犹太界高尚地响应了这一号召，向每一位需要援助的人伸出了援手。我们有权帮助修复同宗教兄弟姐妹破碎的生活，为此必须在正确的方向上不遗余力。这正是难民问题的关键所在。

霍默·马丁（Homer Martin）说，赤色分子渗透工会确有其事。他报告称，虽然其数量被过分强调，但他们作为渗透者的能力却未被夸大。

美国废除禁酒令五年后，饮酒现象明确呈下降趋势。如果禁酒主义者和社会繁荣不登门打扰，美国人或许终将成为一个清醒的民族。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
01759
FES 1 6 1939

The Jews
To the Editor:
A party of German Jews who arrived in Shanghai recently in an Italian liner told a pitiful tale of persecution at the hands of the Nazis and expressed unbounded joy at being in one of the few countries which do not discriminate against their race. This is very flattering; but why are the Jews persecuted? There is hardly a country in the world nowadays which likes them. There must be some reason for it.
This is not to say that Jews haven't very admirable qualities. Everyone can name able Jews; most of us are acquainted with charitable Jews. The vitality of their race impresses everyone who goes to one of their meeting about them which makes it difficult for people to like them.
They should look into themselves and not go about the world exhibiting their self-pity and asking for sympathy. As the "sage" said "The world is for those who know how to live in it." If nobody sympathizes with them, it is no use their demanding sympathy. If a fellow does not like me, it is no use my running to the policeman and asking him to have the fellow arrested. John Bull whom so many people expect to be the world's policeman with the best intentions in the world tried to get the Jews liked in their own ancestral land. He has failed completely.
In what does everybody agree about Jews, even Jews themselves? That they tend to put a higher valuation on moneymaking than most other races. The typical cultured Jew is not the artist who makes art, but the connoisseur who makes money out of art. The musical Jew may attain to a high degree of virtuosity in playing the piano or violin but he never fails to make money out of it. A world famous Jew violinist makes a lot of money out of playing the compositions of Gentiles. Would a Jew respect him as much if he made as little out of music as Beethoven did but wrote his own sonatas?

Lile 8/8
Q 14/2 Q
10/2
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》
01759
1939年2月16日

犹太人
致编辑：
最近乘坐意大利邮轮抵达上海的一群德籍犹太人，讲述了他们在纳粹手中遭受迫害的悲惨故事，并对身处少数几个不歧视其种族的国家之一表达了无限的喜悦。这非常令人受用；但犹太人为何遭受迫害？如今世界上几乎没有哪个国家喜欢他们。这其中必有原因。

这并不是说犹太人没有非常令人钦佩的品质。每个人都能举出能干的犹太人；我们大多数人都认识乐善好施的犹太人。他们的种族活力给每一个参加其聚会的人留下深刻印象，这使得人们难以喜欢他们。

他们应该反省自身，而不是在世界各地展示自怜并乞求同情。正如那位“智者”所说：“世界属于那些懂得如何在其中生活的人。”如果没有人同情他们，他们要求同情也是徒劳。如果某人不喜欢我，我跑去警察那里要求逮捕此人也是无用的。约翰牛（John Bull，指英国）被许多人期望成为世界警察，怀着世上最好的意图试图让犹太人在其祖先的土地上受人喜爱。但他彻底失败了。

关于犹太人，甚至犹太人自己也同意的一点是什么？那就是他们倾向于比大多数其他种族更看重赚钱。典型的有教养的犹太人不是创作艺术的艺术家，而是通过艺术赚钱的行家。犹太音乐家可能在钢琴或小提琴演奏上达到高度的 virtuosity（精湛技艺），但他从不忘记从中赚钱。一位世界著名的犹太小提琴家通过演奏非犹太人的作品赚取了大量金钱。如果他像贝多芬那样从音乐中获利甚微，但创作了自己的奏鸣曲，犹太人还会如此尊重他吗？

Lile 8/8
Q 14/2 Q
10/2

pages.en:
01760

The son of a Jewish friend of
mine who was very wealthy, told
me one day that if he could write
one little poem he would get more
satisfaction out of it than out of
all the moneymaking of his father.
But when his father died he suc-
ceeded to the business and devoted
himself to making money with just
the same, if not more, passion
than his father had done. His
racial tradition was too strong for
him. Jew hates his isolation, but
nobody has isolated him. He has
isolated himself. Americans,
French, Germans, Italians, British,
etc., are not isolated anywhere in
the world; if they find they are
not liked, they work to make
themselves likeable or leave the
countries wherever they may be.
Every civilized person hates the
way Hitler and Mussolini are treat-
ing the Jews because it only serves
to confirm them in their belief
that they are an unfortunate and
persecuted people. But what use
does it do to give them harborage
in some other country? They
merely take their prejudices with
them. The expression; "Come on
don't be a Jew" from boyhood up-
wards; I wonder who invented it?
"ONLOOKER"
Shanghai, Feb. 15, 1939.
* * *
While the foregoing letter im-
presses us of sufficient moderation
and interest to warrant publica-
tion, we must express strong ex-
ception to the suggestion that it
is of no use to give persecuted
people a refuge. Such a thought
must run counter to the attitude
of humanitarians of whatever race
or creed.—EDITOR.
pages.zh:
01760

我的一位非常富有的犹太朋友之子有一天告诉我，如果他能写出一首小诗，他从中获得的满足感将超过他父亲所有的赚钱活动。但当他的父亲去世后，他继承了家业，并以与其父亲相同、甚至更强烈的热情投身于赚钱。他的种族传统对他来说太强大了。犹太人憎恨孤立，但没有人孤立他。是他孤立了自己。美国人、法国人、德国人、意大利人、英国人等在世界任何地方都不受孤立；如果他们发现自己不受欢迎，他们会努力让自己变得讨人喜欢，或者离开所在的国家。每个文明人都讨厌希特勒和墨索里尼对待犹太人的方式，因为这只会坚定他们认为自己是不幸且受迫害民族的信念。但在其他国家为他们提供庇护又有何用？他们只是带着偏见一同前往。“别像个犹太人那样”这句从小听到大的话；我想知道是谁发明的？

“旁观者”
上海，1939年2月15日。
* * *
虽然上述信件给我们留下的印象是其适度性和趣味性足以 warrant（保证）刊登，但我们必须对“给受迫害者提供避难所毫无用处”这一建议表示强烈异议。这种想法必然违背任何人道主义者无论何种种族或信仰的态度。——编者

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY;

FEB 6 1939

The Jewish Refugees
A BITTER outburst against a Jewish
refugee editorial appearing in this paper
a week ago today is published in the latest
issue of the China Weekly Review under the
heading "Jewish Refugees Should Be Wel-
comed And Assisted Here!"
We are charged with having "distinguish-
ed" ourselves "ignobly" for "raising a cry for
the closure of Shanghai to future would-be
Jewish emigrants" and the editorial is said to
have ranged The Post "alongside all those who
express humanitarian sentiments where the
Jews are concerned, but balk at giving
practical aid—if that aid shows signs of cost-
ing them something." We are informed that
in a radio broadcast the previous evening, the
Review's weekly commentator singled the
editor of this paper out for personal mention
as lacking in humanitarian instincts.
"Protesting too much" is always a very
useless business. Likewise for the editor to
embark on personal defense would be misuse
of these columns. We feel it is not out of
order, however, to say that our sentiments
were animated by no lack of full sympathy
with the plight of the refugees but re-
presented a possibly mistaken attitude of
practicality which is shared not by those who
balk at giving practical aid—we know very
few who are not willing to give such aid and
we know few, as a matter of fact, who have
not already contributed in one way or another
—but by those upon whom lies the primary
burden of dealing with this whole problem.
These people we know to be concerned lest the
ever-enlarging "Shanghai quota" swamp them
completely. They are working as the rest of
us are not, in day by day practical efforts
and we feel they are completely right in their
feeling that the position of those already here
is being jeopardised by this unlimited flow.
On Saturday we received by mail from one
of the Jewish relief committee officials a re-
port that 12,000 are now booked for Shanghai.
If true, this bears thinking over.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》；

1939年2月6日

犹太难民
最新一期《密勒氏评论报》在标题为“应欢迎并协助犹太难民来沪！”的文章中，对本刊一周前发表的一篇关于犹太难民的社论进行了激烈的抨击。
我们被指责因“呼吁关闭上海大门以阻止未来潜在的犹太移民”而“卑鄙地”让自己“与众不同”，该社论称本刊“与那些在涉及犹太人时表达人道主义情感、但在援助显示出要让他们付出代价时就退缩的人站在一起”。我们获悉，在前一晚的广播中，《评论报》的每周评论员特别点名提及本报编辑，称其缺乏人道主义本能。

“抗议过甚”总是一件非常无益的事情。同样，编辑进行个人辩护也是对版面的滥用。然而，我们认为不妨指出，我们的情感并非源于对难民困境缺乏充分的同情，而是代表了一种可能错误的务实态度，持有这种态度的并非那些不愿提供实际援助的人——我们知道很少有人不愿意提供此类援助，事实上我们也知道很少有人未曾以某种方式做出贡献——而是那些承担着处理整个问题主要负担的人。我们知道这些人担心不断扩大的“上海配额”会彻底压垮他们。他们日复一日地进行着实际努力，而我们其他人并未如此，我们认为他们完全有理由感到，现有人员的处境正因这种无限制的流入而受到危及。

周六，我们通过邮件收到一位犹太救济委员会官员的报告，称已有12,000人预订前来上海。如果属实，这值得深思。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

FEB 6 1939

It is quite false to portray Shanghai as
the only place on earth for refugees. Other
doors are closed, but there can and will be
provided some more constructive means of
settling these people in places with a chance
for better than necessarily limited charity if
Shanghai says that its capacity for immediate
relief has been reached. When we speak of
capacity for relief we are talking in terms
of the actual possibilities. The committee in
charge might take quite a different attitude
if it could commandeer all of Shanghai's
privately owned wealth. This does not seem
in prospect, to put the matter mildly. The
prospects are inevitably for a diminution of
the flow of help and a corresponding increase
in the misery of poor people who in many
cases come here as a stop-off point and then
find they cannot either move on or make a
living.

It is quite true that Shanghai has a re-
markable record in assimilating refugees.
Many thousands of White Russians have
found means of at least subsistence here and
are respected members of the community to-
day, having arrived with nothing. Even more
thousands of Chinese refugees have been
cared for as result of the war. The Jews who
have already arrived have been treated rather
well, certainly as well as limited resources
permitted. But Shanghai's economic position
today is that of an "isolated island" and it is
clear that there is quite a problem as to
whether existing job opportunities are not due
to dwindle farther, and professional openings
be still more restricted, rather than the con-
verse in any immediate future.

Both municipalities and particularly the
Pivot-supporting International Settlement
should contribute generously to aid for the
Jewish refugees. There are "voluntary"
amusement taxes for Chinese refugees and
there is every reason for extending this help
to the European arrivals. At the same time
charity cannot solve the whole problem and
it is strongly to be hoped that some funda-
mental plan may be worked out in Europe or
the United States for settling the refugees in
a place or places where they will have a
chance to engage in self-supporting activity.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》。

1939年2月6日

将上海描绘为难民在地球上唯一的去处是完全错误的。其他大门虽然关闭，但如果上海宣布其即时救济能力已达极限，那么完全可以并且将会提供更多建设性的手段，将这些人在有机会获得优于必然有限的慈善救济的地方安置下来。当我们谈论救济能力时，我们指的是实际可能性。如果负责委员会能够征用上海所有的私有财富，其态度可能会截然不同。委婉地说，这似乎前景渺茫。前景不可避免地将是援助流动的减少，以及穷人苦难的相应增加，许多人在这种情况下将这里作为中转站，随后发现既无法继续前行也无法谋生。

上海在融合难民方面确实有着非凡的记录，这是千真万确的。成千上万的白俄在这里找到了至少维持生计的方法，并在身无分文抵达后，如今已成为社区中受尊重的成员。更有成千上万的中国难民因战争而得到照顾。已经抵达的犹太人受到了相当好的待遇，至少在有限资源允许的范围内是这样。但上海目前的经济地位是一个“孤岛”，很明显，存在这样一个问题：现有的就业机会在不久的将来是否会进一步萎缩，职业机会是否会更加受限，而非相反。

两个市政当局，特别是支撑核心的公共租界，应慷慨捐助以援助犹太难民。针对中国难民设有“自愿”娱乐税，完全有理由将这种援助扩展至欧洲抵达者。同时，慈善无法解决整个问题，强烈希望能在欧洲或美国制定一些基本计划，将难民安置在一个或多个地方，使他们有机会从事自给自足的活动。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
FEB 4 1938
6220

Jewish Visitors
Expect To Move
To Real Homes

Opportunities Offering
In City For Few
Refugees Only

LOCAL PROBLEM
GETTING WORSE

"THE greater part of Jewish
refugees realize that
they can never find new homes
in Shanghai." This was the
statement of one of the re-
fugees who arrived several
weeks ago from Germany.
"We came here as emigrants
with nothing to lose, for
everything was lost before
departure from Germany."

These former residents of
Germany and Austria are
convinced they will have the
opportunity to travel to other
lands where work may be
obtained more easily than in
Shanghai. They await a help-
ing hand from the United
States, from England, from
South America, from any
place.

In the last three months
two and a half thousand
European Jews have arrived in
Shanghai from Germany. To
further complicate the local
situation is the news of embarka-
tion of 1000 more Jews at Naples,
on January 27, destined for
Shanghai. Most of the emigrants
are said to be members of the
middle classes, merchants, law-
yers, physicians, engineers; all of
whom left behind them profitable
positions.

Step of Distress

As the refugee steps ashore in
Shanghai a fatal step is taken.
In Germany and Austria the
greater part of these people en-
joyed all the comforts of the well-
to-do middle class. Under
financial export restrictions the
refugee could buy his passage and
depart with 30 marks, the
equivalent of US$12. Streng-
thening this control the Govern-
ment has decreed within the last
four weeks that the emigre can
take only 10 marks from his
country.

The passage from Europe to the
Far East is, physically a pleasant
voyage. The four weeks of the
trip pass swiftly, all too rapidly,
for little hope awaits these Jews
at their destination. On board
the steamer they are people of
distinction, but the step from the
ship's tender to the Customs jetty
is a step of distress.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》
1938年2月4日
6220

犹太访客
有望迁入
真正的住所

仅少数难民
在沪有机会

本地问题
日益恶化

“大部分犹太难民意识到，他们永远无法在上海找到新的家园。”这是几周前从德国抵达的一名难民的陈述。“我们作为移民来到这里，已没有什么可失去的，因为在离开德国之前，一切都已经失去了。”

这些前德国和奥地利居民确信，他们将有机会前往其他土地，在那里比在上海更容易找到工作。他们等待着来自美国、英国、南美洲或任何地方的援助之手。

在过去的三个月里，两千五百名欧洲犹太人从德国抵达上海。使本地局势进一步复杂化的是，另有1000名犹太人于1月27日在那不勒斯登船，目的地是上海。据说大多数移民属于中产阶级，包括商人、律师、医生、工程师；他们都放弃了原本有利可图的职位。

痛苦的一步

当难民在上海踏上岸时，便迈出了致命的一步。在德国和奥地利，这些人中的大多数曾享受富裕中产阶级的所有舒适生活。在金融出口限制下，难民可以购买船票，并携带30马克（相当于12美元）离开。为了加强这一控制，政府在过去四周内颁布法令，规定移民只能从本国携带10马克。

从欧洲到远东的航程，在身体上是一次愉快的旅行。四周的旅程过得很快，甚至太快了，因为这些犹太人在目的地几乎没有什么希望可言。在轮船上，他们是受人尊敬的人，但从轮船接驳艇踏上海关码头的那一步，却是痛苦的一步。

pages.en:
Transformation
TRANSFORMED are these emigrants—without food, without money, without prospects—when they land in the new and strange city of Shanghai. True, the relief committee will do what it can. Committee directors and assistants wait for the emigrants at the wharf, but what can be done? After baggage is cleared the men, women and children are loaded into motor lorries and driven to several different places in the city. One group is to live at the Synagogue Beth Aharon on Museum Road, another group goes to the Embankment Building; a few are billeted in private homes. Campbeds, crowded into large rooms, are places of rest for the refugees at the Synagogue and at the Embankment Building. Families are separated in the attempt to provide for all; a modest meal is served. Rigorous discipline becomes the order of the day as everything is organized on an emergency scale. The first move towards a new life has been taken.
Distinguished Emigres
Capital for this new life consists of 30 German marks, only 10 for some; jewelry valued at 150 marks has been brought by a few. Furniture, prized belongings, family treasures collected through years are gone. Among the Jews are distinguished persons, physicians, lawyers and former owners of large industrial plants. The best is made of a bad situation.
Doctors Have Chance
Physicians have a chance of success. No restrictions are placed on this profession in Shanghai and it is only necessary that the doctor notify the Shanghai Municipal Council that he desires to practice medicine. This solves the problem as far as the authorities are concerned, but will there be patients? Perhaps a few will succeed.
Attorneys are not so fortunate. Few of these professional men speak English, and none of them speaks Chinese. Before a law office can be opened it is necessary that the language difficulty be overcome.
Artistic Ability
Musicians, painters, architects and artists are numbered among the refugees. Probably the most fortunate of the group in Shanghai are the musicians for many of these Jews have found work with night club and theatre orchestras. An actor has become a stage manager of a large theatre, another arranges amateur performances, an opera singer gives voice lessons. A famous German newspaper editor is teaching the German language in a private home.
To most of these refugees Shanghai is only a stopping place in their wanderings, searching for a new Fatherland. As there are no immigration restrictions here, no passport visas required, passage here was bought in desperation. What they will do here, how they will arrange life, how and where they will go from Shanghai to answered.
pages.zh:
转变

当这些移民登陆上海这座陌生新奇的城市时，他们发生了转变——没有食物，没有金钱，没有前途。诚然，救济委员会将尽其所能。委员会的董事和助手们在码头等待移民，但又能做什么呢？行李清关后，男人、妇女和儿童被装上汽车卡车，送往市内的几个不同地点。一组人将住在博物馆路（Museum Road）的阿哈龙犹太会堂（Synagogue Beth Aharon），另一组人前往堤岸大厦（Embankment Building）；少数人被安置在私人住宅中。在犹太会堂和堤岸大厦，挤在大房间里的折叠床是难民们的休息之处。为了试图安置所有人，家庭被拆散；供应简单的餐食。随着一切按紧急规模进行组织，严格的纪律成为日常秩序。迈向新生活的第一步已经迈出。

杰出的移民

这种新生活的资本仅为30德国马克，有些人只有10马克；少数人带来了价值150马克的珠宝。家具、珍爱的物品、多年收集的家庭珍宝都已不复存在。犹太人中有杰出人物，包括医生、律师和前大型工厂的所有者。人们在糟糕的境况中尽力而为。

医生有机会

医生有成功的机会。上海对该职业没有限制，医生只需通知上海工部局其希望行医即可。就当局而言，这解决了问题，但会有病人吗？也许少数人会成功。

律师就不那么幸运了。这些专业人士中很少有人会说英语，而且没有人会说中文。在开设律师事务所之前，必须克服语言困难。

艺术才能

难民中包括音乐家、画家、建筑师和艺术家。在上海，这群人中最幸运的可能是音乐家，因为许多犹太人在夜总会和剧院乐团中找到了工作。一名演员成为了一家大剧院的舞台监督，另一名安排业余演出，一位歌剧歌手提供声乐课程。一位著名的德国报纸编辑正在私人家庭中教授德语。

对大多数难民来说，上海只是他们在寻找新祖国过程中的一个停留站。由于这里没有移民限制，不需要护照签证，他们是出于绝望才购买船票来到这里的。他们将在这里做什么，如何安排生活，以及如何以及从哪里离开上海，这些问题尚待解答。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE REGISTRY No. S. R. D. 572-39 2 3 Date..）
FEB 3 1939

Shame!
To the Editor:
"The spirit of the new Germany commands admiration."
Who is speaking? Herr Hitler, Goebbels, Goering, Oswald Mosely, South American demagogues, or other reactionaries? By no means. The quotation, though taken from context, stands by itself and is from —of all places—the editorial columns of the Shanghai Evening Post.
Well, Mr. Editor, the spirit of the new Germany may command your admiration, or the admiration of your solicitors seeking advertisements from local German firms. It commands the admiration of few others, you may be certain.
This spirit of "new Germany" which apparently commands your admiration has persecuted thousands of people, it has made a travesty of culture and science, it has expelled from Germany her finest writers, thinkers, scientists, it has officially claimed women to be put breeding machines, it has propagated phoney racial theories, it proclaims war to be the most commendable manifestation of mankind, it has burned books, it has indulged in a state campaign of bestiality and terror that makes even semi-civilized people shudder. It has muzzled all but official expression and has expelled, jailed, tortured, or executed not a few journalists and I wonder, Mr. Editor, how you would fare in your art in the "new Germany?" From the quotation above, it would appear you would fare well indeed.
For shame, Mr. Editor! Shame on you, also, for suggesting that no more refugees be allowed to land at Shanghai. Shame on you for not having the courage to call spades, for negating American sentiment on the "new Germany" as expressed by a realist you admire, President Roosevelt, and thousands of others! For shame for your blundering?
AMERICAN.
Shanghai, February 2, 1939.
* * *
While shame is being so liberally awarded—shame on our reader for his partial quotation of a paragraph continuing: "But the courses of new Germany's leaders inspire fear and aversion in the hearts of many who want nothing more than friendship of all people."
We repeat that we admire the essential spirit of the new Germany that has struggled out of the post-War despond. That there have been perversions of that spirit is quite another matter.
—EDITOR.

1939年2月3日

羞耻！

致编辑：

“新德国的精神令人钦佩。”

是谁在说话？希特勒先生、戈培尔、戈林、奥斯瓦尔德·莫斯利（Oswald Mosely）、南美的煽动家，还是其他反动分子？绝非如此。这段引文虽然脱离了上下文，但其本身出自——令人惊讶的地方——《上海晚邮报》的社论专栏。

好吧，编辑先生，新德国的精神可能会赢得您的钦佩，或者赢得那些寻求当地德国公司广告的您的广告招揽人员的钦佩。您可以肯定，它很少能赢得其他人的钦佩。

这种显然赢得您钦佩的“新德国”精神迫害了成千上万的人，它使文化和科学变得荒谬可笑，它将德国最优秀的作家、思想家、科学家驱逐出境，它官方宣称女性应沦为生育机器，它传播虚假的种族理论，它宣称战争是人类最值得称赞的表现形式，它焚烧书籍，它 indulge in 一场令即使半文明人也感到战栗的国家兽行和恐怖运动。它钳制了除官方表达以外的所有言论，并驱逐、监禁、折磨或处决了不少记者，我想知道，编辑先生，如果您在“新德国”从事您的职业，境遇会如何？从上述引文来看，您的境遇似乎确实会很好。

真可耻，编辑先生！你也应该感到羞耻，因为你建议不再允许更多难民在上海登陆。你应当感到羞耻，因为你没有勇气直言不讳，因为你否定了一位你所钦佩的现实主义者罗斯福总统以及成千上万其他人所表达的关于“新德国”的美国舆论！为你那笨拙的错误感到羞耻吧？

美国人
上海，1939年2月2日。
* * *
既然“羞耻”被如此慷慨地授予——那么我们的读者也应感到羞耻，因为他片面引用了一段继续写道：“但是，新德国领导人的做法在许多只求与所有人友好相处的人心中引起了恐惧和厌恶。”

我们要重申，我们钦佩新德国从战后消沉中挣扎出来的基本精神。至于这种精神出现了扭曲，那是另一回事。

——编辑

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
FEB 3 1939

Jewish Plight
To the Editor: •
I hope you will excuse if I an-
swer your article in the Jewish
refugee question, even so I was
not asked to do it and also with-
out being worried with all of
them.
If there arrived in any place
in the wide world some thousands
of refugees, there would not be
much excitement about it. If
there are coming a few thou-
sands of Jews we always hear:
there will be much worries.
These few thousands are
desperate, all those men, women
and children. They do not come
here out of love for Shanghai
and their situation is bad enough,
a few excepted.
This situation should be com-
pelling to unite all the forces for
this problem, firstly neutraliza-
tion of assistance for Shanghai.
But it is no solution at all to bar
the open door for people in
desperate situation.
They cannot go to other places
and they cannot stay in Ger-
many. The solution of medical
problems should never result in
the death of the patient.
Just why should Shanghai not
save the world? It does not
make any difference at all who
starts with the saving. In one
point I agree with you, that not
all these people should stay here
for good. With the aid of the
whole world should the problem
be solved.
It is not a matter of humanity
only but of policy, and if Eng-
land and France had not left
Austria in the lurch, at least the
Viennese Jewish people would not
be here.
A PULVERMASTER
Shanghai, Feb. 2, 1939.
* *
The question is not whether
Shanghai "should" save the
world. It is simply that, be-
yond a certain point Shanghai
resources do not reach.—ED.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》
1939年2月3日

犹太人的困境

致编辑：•

我希望您能原谅我回答您关于犹太难民问题的文章，尽管并未有人要求我这样做，我也并未因他们所有人而感到困扰。

如果在世界任何地方有几千名难民抵达，并不会引起太多轰动。如果来的是几千名犹太人，我们总是听到：会有很多麻烦。

这几千人是绝望的，所有的男人、妇女和儿童都是如此。他们来这里并非出于对上海的热爱，除了少数例外，他们的处境已经够糟糕了。

这种情况应该促使各方力量联合起来解决这一问题，首先是中和对上海的援助负担。但是，禁止处于绝望境地的人进入根本不是解决办法。

他们不能去其他地方，也不能留在德国。医疗问题的解决绝不应导致患者的死亡。

为什么上海就不能拯救世界呢？由谁开始拯救根本没有任何区别。在一点上我同意您的看法，即并非所有这些人都应该永久留在这里。这个问题应在全世界的帮助下得到解决。

这不仅是一个人道主义问题，也是一个政治问题，如果英国和法国没有抛弃奥地利，至少维也纳的犹太人就不会在这里。

A PULVERMASTER

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JAN 30 1939

1000 More Refugees
THERE IS SOMETHING almost terrifying in
word that a thousand more Jewish refugees
have sailed from Naples for Shanghai aboard
the Conte Biancamano.
What is going to happen to them?
Local relief has been barely adequate thus
far. It cannot stretch much farther, even for
the people already here. Shanghai is, after all,
a hard-hit city having troubles of its own. With
all due sympathy (and we know there is great
warmth of heart among all classes and nation-
alities in this matter) it is injustice to the
refugees already seeking some sort of foot-
hold here to let further refugees come. And a
thousand on one ship! It's appalling.
Somehow it is going to be necessary to stop
this influx. If no other course presents itself
we recommend an immediate session of the
Consular Body to deal with this alarmingly
growing problem. Shanghai can't save the
world, worse luck.

S
D. S. Pik

《上海晚邮报与信使报》

1939年1月30日

又有1000名难民

有一件事几乎令人恐惧，那就是又有1000名犹太难民乘坐“比安卡马诺伯爵号”（Conte Biancamano）从那不勒斯启航前往上海。

他们将会发生什么？

本地的救济到目前为止仅勉强够用。即使对于已经在这里的人来说，它也难以再大幅扩展。毕竟，上海是一座遭受重创的城市，自有其困难。尽管充满同情（我们知道在此事上各阶层和各国籍人士心中都有极大的热情），但让进一步的难民前来，对已经在此寻求某种立足点的难民来说是不公正的。而且一艘船上就有一千人！这令人震惊。

无论如何，有必要阻止这股涌入。如果没有其他办法出现，我们建议领事团立即召开会议，以处理这一令人 alarmingly 增长的问题。上海无法拯救世界，真是倒霉。

S
D. S. Pik

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JAN 10 1939
Consuls Studying
Refugee Problem

SMC Not Empowered
To Curb Immigrants
For Shanghai

Certain members of the Consular Body in Shanghai have decided to take individual action to stem the influx of European political refugees into the International Settlement and French Concession pending a thorough study of the local refugee situation by the entire Consular Body. At present, Commander L. Neyrone, Consul General for Italy and Senior Consul in Shanghai, is on holiday in Japan. It is understood the Jewish refugee problem will be discussed at the first meeting of the Consular Body on his return to Shanghai.

It is pointed out that no passport regulations are in effect on immigrants or visitors to Shanghai today and that the SMC has gone as far as it can in the matter by notifying the Consular Body and Jewish organizations in Shanghai and abroad of the problems confronting indigent refugees in Shanghai. Action therefore on the SMC's letter to the Consular Body on the Jewish refugee problem will be withheld until the return of the senior consul and a general consular discussion, it is understood.

领事研究
难民问题

工部局无权
遏制赴沪
移民

上海领事团的某些成员决定采取个别行动，以阻止欧洲政治难民涌入公共租界和法租界，直至整个领事团对本地难民情况进行彻底研究。目前，意大利驻上海总领事兼上海首席领事 L. Neyrone 指挥官正在日本度假。据悉，犹太难民问题将在他返回上海后的第一次领事团会议上进行讨论。

有人指出，目前对前往上海的移民或访客没有实施任何护照规定，工部局在此事上已尽其所能，即通知上海及海外的领事团和犹太组织上海贫困难民所面临的问题。因此，据悉，关于工部局致领事团的有关犹太难民问题的信函的行动，将暂缓至首席领事返回并进行一般性领事讨论之后。
